title: Benchmark configurable Synapse inference concurrency
description:
Synapse serializes all inference: one CPU permit (`crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs:171`,
constructed `Semaphore::new(1)` at `:199` and `:224`), one query-admission permit (`:174`),
and one ORT intra-op thread (`crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs:255`). This task
produces a **measurement report and a decision**, not a knob. No production concurrency
parameter is added unless this experiment selects one.

## Mechanisms already established by code reading (to be quantified, not re-derived)

- `Backend::embed` takes `Mutex<TextEmbedding>` (`inference.rs:181`, lock at `:277`), so
  extra CPU permits over one `Backend` cannot parallelize anything; they only move waiting
  from the FIFO semaphore into an unfair `std::sync::Mutex`.
- Batch workers are spawned at admission (`mod.rs:638`) and queue on the *same* FIFO
  `cpu` semaphore as queries (`mod.rs:514`, `:646`). With `max_queued_jobs: 64` and
  `max_batch_items: 64` (`mod.rs:69`, `:71`), one query can wait behind up to 64 full
  batches. This head-of-line coupling — not the absence of parallelism — is the primary
  suspect for query tail under batch load.
- The query-admission permit is held by the worker through the native call, past the
  request deadline (`mod.rs:478-497`), so a timed-out query keeps the query lane closed
  until its native call finishes; a second concurrent query gets `queue_full` (pinned by
  `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_protocol.rs:90`).
- Per-text validation tokenization runs *inside* the model lock (`inference.rs:281-296`)
  before fastembed tokenizes again, so service demand today includes duplicated work
  (owned by `magic-context-chj`; `magic-context-18r` owns only hash/depth preprocessing).

## Phase 0 — prerequisites (blocking; no production source edits)

**0a. Production model artifact provenance.** No production bundle exists in-repo; only
`crates/mc-host/tests/fixtures/synapse-tiny` (8 dims, WordLevel tokenizer), which
`docs/synapse-model-bundle.md` §5 states cannot certify the production model. Installation
is owned by magic-context-c50.8 (in progress). Before any collection, record: bundle
directory, `manifest.model`, `fingerprint`, `dims`, `max_tokens`, `pooling`,
`quantization`, `recommended_batch{rows,token_budget}`, `model_file.sha256`,
`corpus.sha256`, `manifest.provenance`, plus ORT library path, version, target triple and
the pinned `ort_library_sha256` (`SynapseConfig`, `mod.rs:89`). The TypeScript default
local model is `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`
(`packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts:22`); if the Synapse bundle is a
different embedding space, say so — results do not transfer across fingerprints.

**0b. Observability prerequisite.** `magic-context-a52` owns the bounded, fixed-cardinality
Synapse snapshot for CPU-permit wait/hold, native inference time, rejection reason, poll outcome,
and queue/job depth. This experiment is blocked until that contract lands and its overhead is
measured. Harness-side scheduled-send and terminal accounting remains independent. Resource series
come from `/proc/<pid>/status` (`VmRSS`, `VmHWM`), `/proc/<pid>/stat` utime/stime deltas, and
`pidstat -t`. If blocking-pool versus executor delay remains unresolved, invoke
`/performance:tokio-runtime-profiling`; enable `tokio_unstable` only in the measurement artifact,
not as an unreviewed production build change.

**0c. Generator.** `crates/mc-host/examples/perf_load.rs` speaks only `perf-echo`; it has
no `embed.query`/`embed.batch`/`embed.result` arm. Extend it (or add a sibling) reusing its
coordinated-omission-honest accounting (scheduled-send boundary, per-code error map,
scheduler lag) and the `scripts/perf-mc-host.sh` run layout. Store mergeable histograms or
raw sorted vectors; never average percentiles.

## Claim and outcomes

Claim to decide: *for the pinned production bundle, on the target host class, topology T
delivers materially lower query p99 under batch load and/or higher batch deadline goodput
than the single-permit baseline, at a stated RSS/CPU cost, without weakening any bound or
lifecycle guarantee.*

Primary outcome family (declared before collection, two members):
1. query logical-request latency p50/p95/p99, boundary = scheduled send → terminal frame;
2. batch deadline goodput = items published within the client freshness deadline / elapsed.

Every level reports intended / scheduled / sent / admitted / completed / `queue_full` /
`timeout` / `cancelled` counts and `deadline_success_fraction`. Timeouts and rejections are
never dropped from latency; `queue_full` is not goodput. Exploratory: batch job latency,
poll count per job, CPU-seconds per 1k items, RSS peak, shutdown drain time.

## Workload and arrival semantics

- **Query arm — open.** Exogenous fixed-rate scheduled arrivals (interactive search does
  not wait for prior completions), sweep offered λ. Run two variants: no-retry (clean
  rejection accounting) and client-retry-modeled (~100 ms backoff as magic-context-s64
  describes), reporting attempt vs logical-request latency separately.
- **Batch arm — partly open.** Indexing sessions arrive exogenously; within a session,
  chunks are completion-coupled (submit → poll → next). Pin rows per job at
  `recommended_batch.rows` plus {1, 16, 64}; draw token lengths from a real corpus sample.
  fastembed pads each chunk to its longest encoding
  (`fastembed-6.0.0/src/text_embedding/impl.rs:359-372`), so service time scales with
  rows × padded length. Stratify results by token-length class; do not merge classes.
- **Mixed arm — the deciding arm.** Batch submissions at fixed rate + low-rate open query
  load: the head-of-line case created by the shared FIFO permit.
- Warmup: discard the first 10% of the window (baseline contract) and *verify* steady
  state (flat permit-wait, flat RSS), not a fixed iteration count. Ramp down and confirm
  recovery.

## Model and host population

Generalization target is developer machines running the plugin (README: macOS/Windows/
Linux; Synapse itself is Linux-only — `ensure_ort` fails closed elsewhere). The available
box is 128 CPU / 246 GB with 1-minute load spiking above 100, the same hazard
`docs/perf/mc-host-baseline.md` records for Collection 1 — unrepresentative and noisy.
Run every arm inside a pinned CPU budget emulating the target classes: cgroup v2 `cpu.max`
or `taskset`/cpuset at **4, 8, 16** logical CPUs, plus one unrestricted run labeled
exploratory. At 4 CPUs also run a co-tenancy arm with a fixed background CPU load (the
editor/agent the host shares the machine with). Record per run: cores, `cpu.max`, load
before/after, kernel, rustc, commit, ORT sha256, bundle fingerprint.

## Configurations to compare, and rejection conditions

- **B0 baseline** — as-is (cpu 1, query admission 1, intra-op 1). Also the "do nothing"
  candidate: magic-context-s64's admission/backoff fix may close the tail with no
  concurrency change at all.
- **T1 ORT intra-op parallelism** — `with_intra_threads(n)` for n ∈ {2,4,cores}, one call
  at a time (`inference.rs:255` is the only touched line; no weight duplication, no
  lifecycle change). *Reject if:* the fresh bounds do not support the frozen throughput/latency
  claim; post-burst idle CPU or query tails move adversely for the target host class — ORT exposes
  `session.intra_op.allow_spinning` (`ort-2.0.0-rc.13/src/session/builder/impl_config_keys.rs:96`)
  but fastembed's `InitOptionsUserDefined` does not, so spin-wait cannot be disabled
  without bypassing fastembed's builder; or query p99 regresses at the 4-CPU budget from
  ORT threads competing with tokio workers.
- **T2 separate query and batch lanes** — reserve one permit class for queries so queries
  stop queueing behind up to 64 batches. No added parallelism; directly targets the
  measured mechanism; testable with the deterministic engine too. *Reject if* B0's query
  p99 under batch load already meets the target.
- **T3 chunk-level permit release** — batch worker embeds in `recommended_batch`-sized
  chunks, releasing and re-acquiring the permit between chunks to bound head-of-line
  delay. *Reject if* chunking costs material throughput (padding/session overhead) or
  cannot preserve `AbandonGuard` publication semantics (`mod.rs:664-688`).
- **T4 model-instance pool (N backends)** — the only true parallel-inference option.
  *Reject if:* RSS scales ≈N× — weights are deliberately moved into the model once to
  avoid duplicate buffers (`inference.rs:192-196`; bundle cap `MAX_MODEL_BYTES` 2 GiB,
  `bundle.rs:18`) — or startup probe+certification cost ×N is unacceptable, or the 4-CPU
  target cannot pay the footprint.
- **T5 more permits over one backend** — rejected by construction (`Backend` mutex,
  `inference.rs:277`); include only as a control run if the arithmetic must be shown.

## Cost, queue depth, and capacity bound

Per config and per CPU budget: steady `VmRSS`, `VmHWM`, RSS after 60 s idle (arena
retention), CPU-seconds per 1k items, idle CPU for 60 s after the last request, thread
count and per-thread CPU, shutdown drain time. Compute per-resource service demand
`D_cpu` (busy CPU-seconds per completed item) and report the necessary bound
`X ≤ c/D_cpu`; treat it as an upper bound, never an achievable throughput. Do **not** use
`%util` as saturation on a multi-core host — report queue depth plus latency at fixed
offered load. Check Little's Law `E[L] = λ_eff·E[W]` using *admitted* throughput: the query
path is a loss system (fail-fast `queue_full`), the batch path a finite-capacity queue
(K = `max_queued_jobs` 64, server = the FIFO permit). Never convert a mean occupancy into
a permit count; if an overload model is quoted, name it and its invalidators (deterministic
deadlines, retries, non-Poisson arrivals).

## USL applicability

Not applicable to the open query and mixed arms — use the offered-load/goodput curve and
the service-demand bound instead. Admissible only for closed one-request-in-flight sweeps:
T1 over intra-op threads, T4 over pool size with N in-flight batches. Even then require ≥6
levels, independent repeats, randomized order, identical text mix at every level, and
report σ/κ with CIs; refuse coefficient interpretation if residuals show a breakpoint, a
term's CI covers zero (drop to the nested model), error rates move with N, or the fitted
peak lies beyond the measured range.

## A/A control, replication, stopping

- **A/A:** run B0 against B0 through both labels and both schedule slots with an identical
  binary. Report mechanical integrity (binary sha256, bundle fingerprint, ORT sha, run
  completeness) separately from null calibration. `/benchmark-experiment-design` sets the number
  of complete null blocks needed for the chosen statistic. One observed A/A range is not a
  "noise floor".
- **Units:** treatment applied per host process invocation; a block is one complete ordered
  set of configs; the analysis unit is one complete block contrast; requests are
  subsamples. Reset between letters: fresh process, fresh bundle load, fixed idle gap,
  recorded load average. The shared box is the interference boundary.
- **Assignment:** seed-recorded restricted randomization over ABBA-style complete
  templates, template counts differing by at most one. Retain every failed or aborted run —
  a timeout, OOM, or lane-failing outcome may be treatment-dependent.
- **Sizing/stopping:** 3 pilot blocks for paired log-contrast variance, then a fixed block
  count from that pilot; inspect only after a complete block. Two primary outcomes →
  Bonferroni/Holm across the declared family; all other metrics exploratory.

## Required skills and execution order

1. `/quantitative-analysis:statistics-and-benchmarking-discipline` freezes logical request, attempt, service-time, response-time, arrival, outcome, warmup, workload mix, host population, and goodput semantics.
2. `/quantitative-analysis:benchmark-experiment-design` freezes treatment application, randomization and analysis units, A/A controls, block order, replication, uncertainty construction, multiplicity, and stopping before inspecting treatment results.
3. `/performance:perf-pipeline` coordinates baseline, model/runtime/host attribution, specialist routing, human gate before any topology change, and equivalent post-change verification.
4. `/performance:load-test-harness` owns open-loop query and mixed-load sweeps, scheduled-send latency, generator headroom, saturation knee, and recovery ramp-down.
5. `/quantitative-analysis:queueing-theory-for-engineers` consumes the measured arrival and service-demand model to calculate stability, finite-capacity blocking/wait, Little's Law checks, and candidate bounds. It does not choose runtime full behavior.
6. `/quantitative-analysis:usl-scalability-analysis` is allowed only for valid closed-concurrency sweeps with at least six levels and independent repeats. It is not valid for open query or mixed arms.
7. `/performance:tokio-runtime-profiling` separates CPU-permit wait, blocking-pool delay, worker starvation, and work-steal imbalance before blaming model concurrency.
8. `/low-level-systems:scalable-concurrency` owns any selected ownership/topology change. `/low-level-systems:systems-data-structures` is conditional if a permit queue, model pool, or job representation is redesigned; no structure is selected from Big-O alone.
9. `/systems-design:bounded-design` guards capacity, behavior at full, cancellation, deadline, fairness, recovery, and shutdown. `/testing:test-strategy` chooses lifecycle and concurrency tests.
10. `/performance:bench-compare` runs the frozen exact-artifact schedule. No repository pass/fail claim is made without a separately authored performance policy.

## Correctness and lifecycle guards (must hold for any selected topology)

Lane-failure check after permit acquisition and before using a captured backend
(`mod.rs:526`, `:653`); `settle_inference` marking the lane failing before any error
reaches a sink; `AbandonGuard` publication (`mod.rs:664-688`); ordered shutdown
`closing.cancel → close_admission → tracker.close → tracker.wait` (`mod.rs:920-926`) —
report drain time, since N concurrent native calls extend worst case to N × service time;
resident-byte charges held across the native call (`mod.rs:495-497`) unchanged; no starvation
of either request class. Existing guards that constrain any change:
`tests/synapse_protocol.rs:90` (query overload preserves tool-provider capacity) and
`tests/synapse_jobs.rs:446` (graceful shutdown with queued/running/retained jobs).

## Confounds and ordering

Pin one commit for all arms. `magic-context-18r` changes parse/hash demand,
`magic-context-chj` may change tokenization demand, and `magic-context-s64` changes query
admission/poll cadence; any landing mid-collection invalidates cross-config comparison. Record all
three states in the run manifest and rebaseline after any change.

## Stop conditions

Stop and report without adding a knob when any prerequisite is missing: production bundle/ORT identity cannot be pinned; `magic-context-a52` attribution is unavailable or fails its overhead review; the load generator cannot maintain scheduled open load; A/A shows path asymmetry or unstable null behavior; request mix, errors, or service demand change across concurrency levels; or the target host population is undefined. Reject candidates that move waiting behind the `Backend` mutex, exceed resident/RSS or shutdown budgets, starve queries or batches, weaken lane-failure/cancellation invariants, or need unbounded queues. USL coefficient interpretation stops when its applicability checks fail. Without a separately authored repository performance policy, the task ends with evidence and a human decision, not an automatic production change.

## Related work

- `magic-context-a52` blocks measurement: Synapse wait/hold/inference/rejection/poll/depth snapshot.
- `magic-context-c50.8` blocks production artifact/runtime provenance.
- `magic-context-s64` is related: admission/retry/poll policy changes mixed-load results and queue topology.
- `magic-context-18r` changes parse/hash service demand; `magic-context-chj` may change tokenization demand.
- `magic-context-515` is the closed originating audit and model-free baseline.
- `magic-context-bx3` is future GPU work and must not be pulled into this CPU experiment.

## Commands (harness lands in Phase 0)

```
cargo build --release -p mc-host --examples
MC_SYNAPSE_TEST_ORT_LIBRARY=<lib> target/release/examples/synapse_host <data> <bundle> <lib> <sha256>
taskset -c 0-3 ...   # or: systemd-run --user -p AllowedCPUs=0-3 ...
scripts/perf-mc-host.sh docs/perf/runs/synapse-<config> <arm> ...
python <skill>/scripts/exp_design.py size --design paired-log --pilot-contrasts contrasts.csv \
  --null-ratio <claim-owned-boundary> --alternative-ratio <claim-owned-alternative> \
  --alpha <family-allocation> --power <declared-power> --sided <bound-direction>
```

Raw logs plus `env.txt` under `docs/perf/runs/<config>/`; report alongside
`docs/perf/mc-host-baseline.md`.

## Acceptance

A report in `docs/perf/` that: pins bundle fingerprint, ORT identity, commit and CPU
budgets; passes the A/A mechanical and calibration control; reports per config and per CPU
budget the offered/admitted/completed/`queue_full`/timeout counts, query p50/p95/p99 on the
scheduled-send boundary, batch deadline goodput, queue-depth series, CPU-seconds per 1k
items, RSS steady/peak/idle, and shutdown drain; states `X ≤ c/D_cpu`; declares USL
applicability per arm; and ends with one decision — retain the single permit, or adopt
exactly one named topology with its full bound contract (unit, scope, capacity, behavior at
full, wait bound, client-visible feedback code, recovery) and the guard tests it requires.
No production concurrency knob is added unless this report selects one.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned production-bundle experiment with valid A/A, arrival semantics, process-level design, queueing/USL applicability, runtime attribution, CPU/RSS/shutdown costs, and mixed query/batch outcomes produces an evidence-only decision; no concurrency knob lands unless separately approved.

title: Eliminate duplicate Synapse hashing and scalar depth scan
description:
# Eliminate duplicate Synapse hashing and scalar depth scan

Verified against `feat/broca-runner-route` @ `f5f3c463` (synapse sources identical to the reviewed tree). Two *localized, semantics-preserving*
CPU reductions on the Synapse request path. The tokenizer sub-finding is **split out** (see
"Split-out" below) because it needs a real bundle to measure and changes failure taxonomy.

## Verified sub-findings

| # | Site | Fact | Measured cost (this host, 8 MiB batch body) |
|---|------|------|--------------------------------------------|
| B | `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/jobs.rs:180-194` `digest_payload` hashes `item.text` | second full-text SHA-256; first is `protocol.rs:796` `sha256_hex(raw.0.text)` | 4.61 ms of the 4.61 ms digest (99.9%) |
| C | `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/protocol.rs:541-560` string skip uses `iter().position(\|b\| b==b'"' \|\| b==b'\\')` | scalar 2.5 GB/s; `memchr2` is 3-38x faster and already in the dep graph | 3.42 ms -> 90.7 us |

`depth_exceeds` runs on **every** synapse request (`mod.rs:815` -> `protocol.rs:582`), bodies up
to `MAX_BODY_BYTES` = 32 MiB. `digest_payload` runs on every `embed.batch` admission
(`jobs.rs:355`, computed before the table lock). Combined removable CPU on a max-size batch:
~8 ms per request, single-threaded, on the async handler.

## B - drop the text term from the admission digest

### Semantic invariant (oracle)
`payload_digest` decides `Conflict` vs `Existing` at `jobs.rs:375`. Requirement: *two
admissions sharing a `request_key` must produce equal digests iff their payloads are
identical.* Every production admission passes `mod.rs:584`, which rejects
`request_key != canonical_key`, and `canonical_request_key` (`protocol.rs:846-882`) already
binds model, fingerprint, epoch, ordered ids and ordered **recomputed** content hashes. Each
`content_sha256` is recomputed from the text and compared at `protocol.rs:796-799`, so
`content_sha256 == SHA256(text)` holds for every `BatchItem` the protocol builds. Therefore
digesting `(key, id, content_sha256)` per item distinguishes exactly the same payload pairs as
today's digest, unless SHA-256 collides - the same assumption the content-identity ledger
already rests on.

### Minimum change
Delete `update(item.text.as_bytes());` (`jobs.rs:190`) and extend the `digest_payload` doc
comment with the invariant above (recomputed hash stands in for the text; length-prefixed
framing stays, so id/hash boundaries remain unambiguous). No signature, no type, no call-site
change. Expected diff: 1 line of code + comment.

### Guards
- Keep the length prefix (`hasher.update(len.to_le_bytes())`) - removing it would let
  `("ab","c")` alias `("a","bc")`.
- Do **not** delete the digest entirely: `JobTable` is a self-contained unit reached by
  `admit_uncharged_for_tests` and must not assume the caller ran the canonical check.
- Do not touch `canonical_request_key`: it is a cross-language contract with
  `getSynapseBatchRequestKey` (golden vectors in
  `protocol.rs::request_key_matches_the_javascript_golden_vectors`).

### Tests
- Existing must pass unchanged: `synapse::jobs::tests` (replay/conflict/closed at `jobs.rs:865-915`), `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_jobs.rs`,
  `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_protocol.rs:521-545` (conflict matrix), `synapse_roundtrip.rs`.
- Add one unit test in `jobs.rs::tests`: same key, same ids, **different `content_sha256`**
  -> `AdmitOutcome::Conflict`; byte-identical items -> `AdmitOutcome::Existing`. The existing
  conflict case differs only in id/text with a constant `"0".repeat(64)` hash, so it does not
  pin the post-change discriminator.

## C - `memchr2` for the in-string skip

### Semantic invariant (oracle)
`depth_exceeds` must stay byte-identical in verdict to today for every input, including:
delimiters inside strings never count; backslash consumes exactly one following byte
(parity); an unterminated string returns `false` and leaves syntax reporting to serde; keys
count like values; scalars count one level below their container.

### Minimum change
Add `memchr = "2"` to `crates/mc-host/Cargo.toml` (**already in `Cargo.lock` as 2.8.2 via
`serde_json`** - no new crate in the graph, no new build unit) and replace the inner
`body[index..].iter().position(...)` (`protocol.rs:542-545`) with `memchr::memchr2(b'"', b'\\', &body[index..])`.
Nothing else: the outer structural dispatch runs only at token boundaries, and for
`embed.batch` bodies almost every byte is inside a string, so one call covers the bulk.
`index == body.len()` yields an empty slice, which `memchr2` handles. Expected diff: 1 dep
line + 1 expression.

### Tests
Existing `protocol.rs::tests` depth cases (`depth_eight_passes_and_depth_nine_fails`,
`delimiters_inside_strings_never_count_toward_depth`,
`a_scalar_at_the_container_limit_is_one_level_deeper`,
`depth_counts_params_that_precede_method`) plus `tests/protocol_vectors.rs`. Add a
differential property test (loop over ~10k pseudo-random bodies from a seeded LCG over the
alphabet `{ } [ ] " \ , : space x \n }`) asserting the retained scalar reference and the
`memchr2` version agree; keep the reference `fn` in `#[cfg(test)]` so the oracle is permanent.
Seed printed on failure. This is the check that a hand-audited escape-parity change needs.

## Benchmark protocol (both sub-findings)

- **Harness**: one new `crates/mc-host/benches/synapse_preprocess.rs`. No new dependency:
  `criterion` is absent from the workspace and is not needed for two kernels. Use a
  `#[bench]`-free plain `fn main` bench binary (`[[bench]] harness = false`) with
  `Instant`, `std::hint::black_box`, raw block output, artifact hashes, and environment metadata.
- **Design**: `/benchmark-experiment-design` fixes warmup evidence, treatment order, process-level
  analysis units, independent block count, interval construction, and stopping before fresh
  collection. Repetitions inside one process are subsamples and cannot expose build/allocator/layout
  effects. Report absolute values, paired ratios and uncertainty, not only a best/min time.
- **Treatments**: (1) scalar baseline = today's code, (2) candidate. For B also record
  (3) `hashes-only digest` vs (4) `no digest at all` as a floor, to show the residual is
  ~1 us and not worth further work.
- **Workloads (size classes)**: 756 B single-item body; 64 KiB / 16 items x 4 KiB (typical
  chunk mix); 8 MiB / 64 items x 128 KiB (`max_batch_text_bytes` shape); one escape-dense
  variant (`\n` every 64 B) as the adversarial case for C - escapes bound the win at ~4.8x.
- **Baselines to beat, not skip**: scalar `position` (C), `sha2` at its SHA-NI rate
  (B: 1.82 GB/s measured, so the digest is already hardware-fast - the win is *not hashing
  the text at all*, never a faster hash). Do not swap SHA-256, do not add `asm`/`force-soft`
  features, do not evaluate non-cryptographic hashes: the digest output feeds an identity
  decision and the content hash is a wire contract.
- **Allocation / copy measures**: assert in the bench binary with a counting
  `GlobalAlloc` wrapper that (a) `depth_exceeds` performs **zero** allocations before and
  after, (b) `digest_payload` performs zero, (c) no additional byte copy of item text is
  introduced anywhere. Also record peak RSS delta for the 8 MiB case; both changes must be
  RSS-neutral (they only *remove* reads).
- **Decision and stop conditions**:
  - Freeze the workload-specific materiality claim and smallest important effect before fresh
    treatment collection. The pilot numbers above may size the experiment but must not become a
    post-hoc repository policy.
  - For C, report the full size/escape distribution and uncertainty. Stop if small-body cost moves in
    the wrong direction or the maintained-library path does not improve representative large bodies.
  - For B, stop if any idempotency verdict changes or the fresh run does not show that removing the
    second text pass reduces representative batch CPU.
  - Without a separately authored repository performance policy, present evidence for human approval;
    do not auto-classify a pass from an invented percentage.
  - Either sub-finding being rejected does **not** block the other; land only approved work.
  - No further optimization of these two functions after their gate passes. Do not proceed to
    a vectorized structural scanner, a SIMD JSON depth pass, hand-written intrinsics,
    `#[target_feature]`, or runtime dispatch. Those require a *new* representative profile and the
    `/simd-optimize` need, population, and amortization gates. `memchr` already carries SSE2/AVX2 and
    NEON dispatch; a custom kernel would duplicate maintained code and add an unsafe-review
    burden for no measured need.

## Required skills and execution order

1. `/performance:perf-pipeline` owns orchestration, baseline provenance, evidence routing, and final verification. Static findings remain hypotheses until the frozen microbench confirms them.
2. `/quantitative-analysis:statistics-and-benchmarking-discipline` freezes workload classes, timing boundary, warm/cold state, outcomes, estimand, target host population, and reporting contract before collection.
3. `/quantitative-analysis:benchmark-experiment-design` fixes process-level units, A/B order, A/A control, replication, interval construction, and stopping. Inner iterations are subsamples, not independent runs.
4. `/performance:performance-analyzer` rechecks frequency, allocation, copy, and async-worker impact at current HEAD before editing.
5. `/performance:hashing-prng-and-checksum-speed` owns the SHA-256 semantic contract and verifies that the win comes from removing the redundant text pass, not weakening the stable cryptographic identity.
6. `/performance:simd-optimize` owns the depth-scanner implementation level. Its zero-dispatch ladder applies: use maintained `memchr2`; custom intrinsics, `#[target_feature]`, or runtime dispatch are forbidden unless a new post-change profile passes need, population, and amortization gates.
7. `/low-level-systems:systems-data-structures` is conditional only. Invoke it if implementation proposes changing `BatchItem`, `JobTable`, indexing, or resident layout. Current localized changes do not justify a representation redesign.
8. `/testing:test-strategy` selects differential/property and protocol integration tests; `/implementation:rust-implementation` applies the approved minimal edits.

## Portability
`memchr` 2.8.2: `std` + runtime x86-64 SSE2/AVX2 and aarch64 NEON dispatch with a portable
fallback, so no `RUSTFLAGS`, no `target-cpu`, no `cfg` fork, and no behavioural difference
across hosts. `sha2` 0.10.9 already autodetects SHA-NI through `cpufeatures`; both changes are
arch-neutral. Numbers above are from AMD EPYC 9R14 (Zen 4, sha_ni/avx2/avx512f), rustc 1.97.1,
`-O`; on a host without AVX2 expect a different ratio; the fresh target-host run reports it without assuming a fixed speedup.

## Non-goals (explicitly out of scope; do not bundle)
- Tokenizer pre-pass, tracked separately by `magic-context-chj`.
- `sha256_hex` hex formatting (`protocol.rs:888-895`, 32 `write!` calls) and
  `canonical_request_key`'s two `json_string` allocations per item. Measured: hex encoding is
  451 ns of the 1612 ns spent hashing one 2 KiB chunk (28%); a safe lookup-table encode is
  45.6 ns. Real but a constant factor, not a duplicate pass. File separately if wanted; the
  golden-vector tests already cover it, so it is ~5 lines with no new test burden.
- No change to `parse_reservation_bytes` or the resident-byte ledger: neither change alters
  peak allocation, so the reservation constants stay valid.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `digest_payload` no longer reads `item.text`; its doc comment states the
   recomputed-hash invariant.
2. `depth_exceeds` uses `memchr::memchr2`; `memchr` is a direct dependency and
   `Cargo.lock` gains **no** new package.
3. `cargo test -p mc-host` passes with no expectation edited except the added tests;
   `cargo clippy -p mc-host --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean.
4. New tests: (a) digest conflict discriminated by `content_sha256`, (b) seeded differential
   property test scalar-vs-`memchr2` over >= 10k random bodies.
5. `crates/mc-host/benches/synapse_preprocess.rs` committed, reporting for each size class:
   treatment medians, paired ratio + bootstrap CI, process count, allocation counts, host,
   commit, rustc version. Fresh evidence and the human decision are recorded in the task note.
6. No behaviour change observable on the wire: `synapse_protocol.rs`, `synapse_jobs.rs`,
   `synapse_roundtrip.rs`, `protocol_vectors.rs` unchanged and green.

## Related work

- `magic-context-chj`: split-out production-bundle measurement and safe tokenization change.
- `magic-context-a52`: Synapse wait/hold/inference attribution consumed by later whole-request analysis.
- `magic-context-ioi`: concurrency experiment must pin whether this task landed and rebaseline if needed.
- `magic-context-vho`: resident parse accounting is separate and must not be changed here.
- `magic-context-515`: originating performance audit.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh process-level comparison and protocol tests validate removing the second full-text digest pass and replacing scalar quote/backslash search with maintained memchr2; identity, depth, allocation, wire, and portability invariants hold; tokenizer work remains split to magic-context-chj.

mc-host: anchor lifecycle transaction lock to the evidence namespace
description:
Codex review of PR #21 (comment 3837084109): the KTD2 lifecycle-root lock inode is a mutual-exclusion token only. If ${dataDir}/cortexkit/lifecycle is renamed while a transaction holds the lock, a second caller recreates the path and locks a fresh inode, and two mutating transactions overlap on the same sibling run/ evidence — the lock descriptor anchors no evidence operations.

Blast radius today is bounded: no production mutator takes acquire_exclusive yet (launcher work is U2+, gated on c50.12/c50.4), and the evidence writes are individually fenced (instance lock + atomic identity-fenced writes), which is also why probes tolerate running with no root lock. But the serialization guarantee the doc claims for future launcher transactions does not survive path replacement.

Fix direction: make mutating transactions operate through a descriptor anchored by the locked inode (e.g. lock the runtime directory inode itself, or resolve evidence paths relative to the locked directory and re-verify identity), and update protocol 4.3 accordingly. Should land with or before the first production acquire_exclusive caller (U2+).

title: Memory transmutation suggestions (dreamer task, suggestions-only)

Knowledge should graduate out of prompt prose into stronger artifacts. New dreamer task scanning verified memories and proposing — never applying — a stronger representation:

- PROJECT_RULES -> proposed CI/commit guard (suggestion text only, no generated enforcement)
- NAMING -> proposed lint rule
- ARCHITECTURE -> proposed ADR / doc section (extends existing maintain-docs task)

Surfaced like smart notes at natural boundaries. On acceptance, the memory shrinks to a compact pointer + artifact ref (test path, lint rule id, ADR link) — prompt budget shrinks while knowledge gets stronger.

Hard rule: LLM-extracted memories never auto-become enforcement. Suggestions only until acceptance-rate data justifies more.

## Measure

Suggestion acceptance rate; whether accepted artifacts later catch regressions; net prompt-token reduction from archived memories.

title: [epic] Action-triggered memory: anti-memory, failure signatures, JIT interrupts
description:
The differentiator line vs generic memory providers: surface prior rejections, failure lessons, and safety constraints at the moment the agent is about to repeat them — not as generic prompt injection. Three tasks, strictly sequenced: content types first (anti-memory, failure signatures), the action-hook surfacing layer last.

Guardrails for the whole line: warn-only (never block), hard per-turn budget, expiry/revalidation via dreamer so warnings don't calcify into stale institutional fear. Measured by repeated-rejected-approach rate, repeated-failure rate, and false-warning rate — a noisy interrupt system is worse than none.

title: Anti-memory: typed rejected-approach records
description:
Rejected ideas are currently deleted or buried in narrative compartments; retrieval of "we already rejected Redis" depends on luck. Give rejections a first-class type.

## Scope

- Record: trigger (semantic scope of work), rejected_strategy, rejection_reason, safer_alternative (optional), scope, valid_from/valid_until, evidence refs. Rides the claims schema (U6) + bitemporal/trust columns (U6c/3q5.32).
- Sources: explicit user rejections, dreamer retrospective corrections (existing task already harvests these — this types its output), approaches abandoned after failure.
- Surfacing: as a warning fragment when ctx_search / auto-search-hints matches semantically similar work. Warn-only. Later consumed by the JIT interrupt layer.

title: Replace notes_fts trigram projection with bigram top-K dominance-walk engine (19x, search-lab validated)
description:
Replace the `notes_fts` trigram-FTS5 candidate projection with the bigram + top-K dominance-walk engine validated in the search-lab worktree (branch `search-lab`, `experiments/search-lab/`). Measured against a mirror of the production contract on a 12k-doc corpus: recall\@10 held at 100% of the production scorer's golden results, p95 candidate+rank latency 7.56ms -> 0.38ms (~19x), index bytes 35.3MB -> 16.4MB (2.2x). Full evidence: `experiments/search-lab/FINDINGS.md` on that branch; iteration ledger in the worktree's `autoresearch-results.tsv` (5 keeps / 12 discards, every alternative measured and falsified — hybrid trigram postings, dense-gram pruning, Roaring bitmaps, suffix array, galloping intersection all lost).

## Why this wins

The production scorer (`rankNotesForNeedle`, search.ts) computes `score = 2*exact + m/n + 0.5*(m=n>1)` with id-ascending tie-break — discrete and monotone in `(exact, m)`. The winning engine (`experiments/search-lab/engines/topk-walk.ts`) exploits this:

1. Bigram postings (sorted Uint16Array doc ids) generate exact-substring candidate supersets by rare-first intersection of at most 4 rarest grams; bigrams natively serve the 2-char needles that currently force `noteFtsQueryForNeedle` to return null and trigger a full `scopedNoteScan`.
2. Exact-token postings answer coverage (`m`) via binary search.
3. Candidates are walked in score-bucket dominance order (exact ∧ m=n first, token-only m=1 last), pulling ids ascending with early exit at K — the engine returns exactly K provable-top-K ids instead of feeding thousands of candidates to the scorer. Single-token needles: first K ids of the token posting, O(K), zero verification.
4. Lazy substring verification (`.includes` on prelowered text) only until K results exist. Keep native `.includes` — a JS fold-scan measured 5x slower; the prelowered store earns its bytes.
5. WORK_BUDGET fallback to plain superset union keeps pathological needles correct.

## Scope

- Add the posting index as a derived in-memory structure over searchable notes, built from SQLite (system of record — unchanged) on first search / startup, updated or invalidated on note write. Note cardinality is thousands: full rebuild is milliseconds-scale; do not build snapshot persistence.
- Replace `loadNoteSearchCorpus`'s FTS candidate path (`selectNoteCandidateIds` + `noteFtsQueryForNeedle`) with the engine; keep `scopedNoteScan` as the fallback for engine-unrepresentable needles (len<2) and error paths (matches the engine's own contract).
- `rankNotesForNeedle` stays the ranking authority. CRITICAL COUPLING: the engine's bucket order reproduces the scorer's dominance structure — if scoring changes, the walk must change with it. Port the lab's golden-set recall test (engine top-K vs full-scan scorer top-K on a seeded corpus, must be 100%) as the regression guard; add a property-style test comparing engine output to `scopedNoteScan`+`rankNotesForNeedle` over randomized needles.
- Retire `notes_fts` + `notes_search_view` (migrations.ts:239-251, migration 2900) only after the engine path is proven — follow the repo's FTS retirement discipline (see KTD29 note on 3q5.18: legacy query paths may need to outlive their replacement's flag).
- Coordinate with 3q5.18 (U17 dual lexical indexes): that unit rebuilds the retrieval_documents lexical lanes; this task owns only the notes candidate projection. The identifier-lane design there cites trigram — the lab evidence (bigram + dominance walk >> trigram FTS) should inform U17's identifier index choice.

## Non-goals

- No new dependencies, no LMDB/RocksDB (measured unnecessary at this cardinality; see FINDINGS.md "embedded DB" section).
- No change to message FTS (`message_history_fts`), RRF fusion, probe weighting, or the workspaced search union.

## Acceptance

- Golden-set recall test: engine candidates reproduce production top-K at 100% on the seeded corpus.
- Randomized equivalence test vs scoped-scan path passes.
- Existing search tests (search.test.ts, 3988-test plugin suite) green with zero behavioral diffs.
- Measured candidate-path latency improvement on a representative corpus recorded in the PR description (lab predicts ~19x at 12k docs).
- 2-char needle path no longer full-scans (test exists today at search.test.ts:2159 asserting the fallback — it must be updated to assert indexed behavior).
notes: RETIREMENT GATE (KTD29, per review): notes_fts + notes_search_view retire only after magic-context-3q5.19's RRF-cutover flag itself retires — not merely after the bigram engine path is proven. 3q5.19's flag-off path promises byte-identical legacy ranking across all sources, which needs the pre-cutover notes lexical surface intact. Implementation of the engine may proceed independently; only the drop step is gated.

title: U20: Reranker cascade (explicit search)
description:

## Goal
Optional quality lift where latency is tolerable.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R11: bounded work.
- R15 boundary (fusion stays the ranking scheme; reranking is a cascade on top for explicit search).
- KTD15: "Reranking is a cascade, explicit search only: cheap contiguous SoA feature model over all candidates -> cross-encoder only for the uncertainty set where score intervals overlap -> token-length batching and a hard deadline. Auto-search never pays reranker latency; it uses exact lookup + FTS + dense + fusion + a conservative confidence gate."

title: U17: Dual lexical indexes (parallel-build swap)
description:
Phase 4. BENCHMARK-GATED (via U16's U5 dependency): U5 gates ranking changes; lexical-category metrics must be >= baseline.

RETIREMENT ORDER (KTD29 — note carried on both U17 and U18): "U17's old lexical tables and query paths stay live until U18's RRF-cutover flag itself is retired, not until U17's own backfill completes. U18's flag-off test promises byte-identical legacy ranking; that promise needs the pre-cutover lexical surface intact, so U17 cannot drop storage-memory-fts.ts's query paths on its own schedule."

## Goal
Prose and identifier lexical lanes replace Porter-everything.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R18: "Lexical retrieval has two representations over the retrieval projection: a prose FTS index without unconditional Porter stemming with per-column BM25 weights, and an identifier/path index (trigram or custom token characters) plus exact lookup tables; natural-language queries are never strict all-token conjunctions."
- R8: migration discipline (zero dark-search windows).
- KTD5: "FTS tokenizer changes are parallel-build swaps. Build the new-tokenizer table alongside (*_fts_v2 naming), backfill, swap atomically, drop the old table; a migration test asserts search returns results throughout. Tokenizers cannot be ALTERed on FTS5 tables." (Old-table drop applies to the swapped table; the legacy QUERY PATHS survive until U18's flag retires per KTD29.)
- KTD24: "The U17 FTS parallel-build swap uses a high-water-mark catch-up, not a point-in-time backfill snapshot. The backfill records the last-applied outbox position; once the initial backfill completes, a final catch-up pass replays every mutation after that position before the atomic rename — closing the gap where a write lands in the old table during a long backfill and never reaches the new one."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/lexical-index.ts (+ test)
- memory/storage-memory-fts.ts query paths STAY LIVE per KTD29 (retired with U18's flag, not by this unit)

## Approach
1. Prose FTS over retrieval_documents with unicode61 (no Porter) and per-column BM25 weights (title/claim 5-10x, rationale 2-3x, body 1x).
2. Identifier index: trigram FTS table (case-preserving) plus exact lookup tables for paths/SHAs/IDs/symbols extracted by the projection writer.
3. Parallel-build swap per KTD5 for any table replacing an existing FTS surface; multiple candidate lists per query (exact phrase, identifier, high-signal conjunction, broader disjunction, prefix/NEAR) generated from the U16 AST — never one all-token conjunction.
4. High-water-mark catch-up per KTD24 (quoted above).

## Test scenarios
- Migration test proves CONTINUOUS search: results present before, during (old table still serving), and after the swap on a seeded corpus (zero dark-search windows).
- Concurrent-write coverage: mutations applied to the old table during the backfill window are ALL present in the new table after the swap (the KTD24 catch-up closes the gap a point-in-time backfill would miss).
- Identifier recall: foo::bar and a path substring match via trigram where Porter-tokenized FTS missed them (regression pair fixture).
- Multilingual prose (non-English fixture) matches under unicode61 where the Porter-stemmed index failed.
- BM25 column weighting: a title hit outranks a body-only hit for the same term.
- Broad disjunction list recalls a document the strict conjunction missed; fusion (U18) ranks it sanely.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark lexical-category metrics >= baseline.

title: U18: Global weighted RRF cutover + progressive deepening
description:
Phase 4. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates ranking changes. THE CUTOVER'S GATE: fused metrics >= baseline on the judged corpus, measured on the FINAL PACKED and deduplicated output (post-U19), not raw candidate lists (Success Criteria: a benchmark pass on candidates that U19's packing then discards would not reflect what auto-search actually delivers).

FLAG LIFECYCLE (KTD29 — note carried on both U17 and U18): while this unit's cutover flag exists, U17's pre-cutover lexical tables and query paths stay live for the flag-off path. When the flag retires, the legacy scoring path is REMOVED (not flag-parked, per Definition of Done) and U17's old query paths retire with it.

## Goal
One coherent ranking scheme across all sources.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R15: "Cross-source ranking uses global weighted reciprocal-rank fusion; cosine, BM25, and synthetic scores are never mixed arithmetically, and the static source boosts (memory 1.3 / message 1.15 / commit 1.2 / primer 1.25) are removed."
- R16: "Trust and contradiction rules are hard filters, never soft relevance features; a highly similar contradicted claim is excluded, not down-ranked."
- R19: "RRF lanes deepen progressively: start with small per-lane candidate sets and stop when the maximum possible RRF contribution of unseen documents cannot overtake the current k-th result."
- KTD6: "RRF cutover is all-or-nothing per search call behind a single flag ... New sources (tool events) ship only under the new fusion."
- KTD18: "RRF lane weights start at 1.0 (uniform) across all lanes and are tuned only through the U5 benchmark, never by ad hoc per-source multipliers ... one versioned lane-weight table, checked in next to the benchmark snapshots, changed only when a benchmark run shows a specific lane's weight change improves nDCG@10 without regressing another lane."
- KTD19: "Trust and conflict filtering runs during lane construction, before ranks feed RRF — never after fusion ... The corrected order is LEX/DENSE lanes -> TRUST (per-lane eligibility) -> FUSE -> HYD." (This corrects the plan's earlier FUSE -> TRUST diagram ordering — an excluded contradicted candidate must not occupy a rank slot that shapes surviving documents' RRF scores.)

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts (+ test)
- config flag in packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts

## Approach
1. Replace 0.7 x cosine + 0.3 x reciprocal-rank, the single-source penalty, and the static source boosts with score(d) = sum over lanes of w_i / (k + rank_i(d)), k = 60 (consistent with the existing message/compartment RRF); w_i starts uniform 1.0 per KTD18.
2. Trust/conflict eligibility runs PER LANE before rank positions feed the fusion sum (KTD19) — an excluded candidate can never shape a surviving document's score.
3. Progressive deepening operates over eligible (post-trust-filter) ranks only: start 8-16 candidates per lane; stop when the max possible contribution of unseen eligible documents (sum of w_i/(k + next_rank_i)) cannot overtake the current k-th; deepen only unresolved lanes.
4. All-or-nothing flag per KTD6; auto-search additionally applies a conservative confidence gate before emitting a hint. The flag-off path uses U17's still-live pre-cutover lexical surface.

## Test scenarios
- Cross-source fixture: a document ranked #1 in two lanes outranks a single-lane #1 regardless of raw score magnitudes; no score-scale coupling (change one lane's raw scores, ranks unchanged).
- Deepening stop rule discriminated in BOTH directions: fixture where lane 2's unseen eligible max cannot overtake — assert lane 2 is NOT deepened; opposite fixture deepens it and changes the result.
- A contradicted claim with the highest cosine similarity never ENTERS a lane's eligible rank list, so it cannot affect fusion scores or appear in results (stronger than "absent from output" — proves the KTD19 ordering).
- Refill correctness: a candidate excluded by trust filtering after the initial 8-16 window is fetched does not silently shrink the returned count below the requested K — the eligible pool backfills before the stop rule locks in.
- Flag off -> BYTE-IDENTICAL legacy ranking, using U17's still-live pre-cutover lexical surface (guards the cutover).
- Auto-search gate: weak fused confidence emits no hint.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark fused metrics >= baseline on the judged corpus, measured on final packed/deduplicated output (post-U19).
notes: KTD29: while the cutover flag exists, U17 pre-cutover lexical surface stays live for flag-off; at flag retirement the legacy scoring path is REMOVED, not parked; reduce-complexity: one flag + one formula replaces three scoring mechanisms; less-code: net deletion at flag retirement; perf: progressive deepening bounds lane work (R19); ponytail-review: uniform w_i=1.0 start tuned only via benchmark (KTD18) - no hand-tuned boosts return; invariant-test-review: KTD19 ordering proven by never-enters-eligible-list oracle (stronger than absent-from-output), deepening rule discriminated in BOTH directions, refill correctness, flag-off byte-identity; test-strategy: constructed discriminating fixtures + byte-identical golden for flag-off

title: U16: Query analyzer + planner + index-time DF
description:
Phase 4 — Query pipeline and ranking. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; verification requires no quality regression vs baseline on the judged corpus for lexical-heavy categories.

## Goal
One lexer + AST drives every lane; plans avoid work.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R17: "A deterministic query analyzer lexes queries into typed atoms (memory ID, commit SHA, file path, symbol, error code, quoted phrase, prose) and selects a plan per query; exact identifiers resolve via indexed lookup without embedding, and dense retrieval is skipped or deferred when lexical confidence is strong."
- KTD8: "The query analyzer is one maximal-munch lexer producing typed atoms and a query AST reused everywhere — exact lookup, FTS query formation, dense gating, highlighting, fusion weighting, packing coverage. Document frequencies are maintained at index time (exact hashed counts for important atoms; a Count-Min Sketch is acceptable where overestimation only downweights a probe) — no query-time posting-count queries. Extends packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/literal-probes.ts rather than a parallel implementation."
- KTD23: the query-atom cap (landed in U3) is enforced in THIS lexer before planning.

## Key files
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/query-analyzer.ts (+ test), absorbing/extending literal-probes.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts
- DF bookkeeping in the projection writer (retrieval-projection.ts)

## Approach
1. Maximal-munch lexer -> typed atoms (memory ID, SHA, file path, symbol including camelCase/underscore/namespaced forms, error code, quoted phrase, temporal term, prose word); the AST is reused for exact lookup, FTS query formation, dense gating, highlighting, fusion, packing coverage.
2. Plan selection: exact IDs -> indexed lookup, no embedding; rare atoms with strong margin -> FTS first, dense skipped/deferred; mixed -> lexical first, dense conditional; prose -> parallel lanes. Dense embedding no longer starts unconditionally.
3. DF maintained at index time (exact for important atoms, CMS acceptable); no query-time posting counts.

## Test scenarios
- Lexer goldens: scaleConvolveVSym3, foo::bar, CR-297402306, packages/plugin/src/search.ts, HTTP_503, quoted phrases, mixed prose+identifier queries — each yields the expected atom types; identifiers are NOT split at underscores/dots.
- Memory-ID query plan performs ZERO embedding calls (provider spy).
- Rare-atom query with strong lexical margin skips the dense lane; an ambiguous query runs both.
- DF counts update on document add/remove; CMS overestimation only ever DOWNWEIGHTS a probe (property assertion on probe weighting).
- Empty and whitespace-only queries return empty plans without lane execution.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark shows no quality regression vs baseline on the judged corpus for lexical-heavy categories.
notes:
reduce-complexity: one lexer reused by every lane REPLACES parallel probe logic - net complexity reduction; less-code: extends literal-probes.ts rather than a parallel implementation (KTD8); perf: index-time DF kills query-time posting scans, plans avoid work (dense no longer unconditional); ponytail-review: CMS only where overestimation is safe - already scoped; invariant-test-review: CMS safety proven as a property (overestimation only downweights), zero-embedding plan proven via provider spy; test-strategy: golden lexer examples + property for CMS + spy-based plan assertions
DELTA (future-enhancements review): the planner emits ABSTAIN as a first-class plan outcome (low top-score margin + low lane agreement + unresolved claim conflict) instead of always returning best-effort results. Benchmark-gated via the must-abstain canary category added to U4.

title: U15: Benchmark-gated layout/cascade/batching variants
description:
Phase 3. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; every variant here lands ONLY on a measured win vs the U10 baseline (R28). Success-criteria coupling: the 128 MB decoded-index target is CONTINGENT on a U15 compressed variant winning its recall gate; if none passes, the memory threshold relaxes to the f32 baseline (~154 MB) and R12's ANN trigger fires (ANN itself stays deferred/trigger-gated — no HNSW work here).

title: U13: Module routes + TS client + queues/cancellation
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
The engine is reachable from both harnesses with deadlines, priorities, a transparent fallback, and a caller-authorization boundary that cannot be bypassed by a mis-scoped filter or a coalesced request.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R11: bounded, cancellable, priority-aware; "interactive queries have reserved capacity that backfills and background work cannot consume."
- R13: "Search stays functional when the Rust engine is unavailable (daemon down, rust mode off, index cold): the TypeScript scan path remains a working fallback, and cold-start windows degrade transparently."
- R32: "The dense search route derives a caller's authorized project/session/trust scope server-side and never trusts a caller-supplied filter as authorization; every coalescing key (singleflight, result cache) includes that authorized scope so two callers with the same query text but different scope never share a scan or a cached result."
- KTD25: "Singleflight and the generation-keyed result cache key on the authorized scope, the complete normalized filter set, the embedding space, and the generation id together — never on (embedding_space, normalized_query_hash) alone." Plan risk note: this key shape is a correctness requirement, not a performance nicety.
- KTD1 (routes on the existing ck-mc module; subc transport 0.28-0.38 ms p50), KTD3 (dedicated compute pool; cancellation between scan blocks), KTD16 (the native ctx_search facade in crates/mc-module/src/memory_tool.rs routes through the SAME engine; divergences documented per PARITY.md conventions only when mechanism, not behavior, differs).

## Key files
- crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs (route registration), new crates/mc-module/src/vector_search.rs, crates/mc-module/src/memory_tool.rs
- packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-transport.ts
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search-backend.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts

## Approach
1. vector.search route: accepts query text or vector, filters, K, embedding-space identity, deadline; inference, normalization, scan, top-K stay daemon-side; cancellation checked between scan blocks.
2. Per KTD25: derive the caller's authorized project/session/trust scope server-side and intersect it with requested filters; coalescing keys include authorized scope + complete normalized filter set + embedding space + generation id.
3. Bounded interactive and background queues with reserved interactive capacity.
4. TS search-backend.ts seam: RustVectorBackend (route) and TsScanBackend (current scalar path) behind one interface; automatic fallback on connection failure/staleness per module-transport.ts conventions; a cold daemon serves the TS fallback while segments load, then flips.
5. Native ctx_search facade routes through the same engine (KTD16).

## Test scenarios
- Route round-trip on the hermetic daemon harness (packages/e2e-tests/src/rust-harness.ts, crates/mc-module/tests/real_daemon.rs): identical results TS-fallback vs Rust route on a seeded corpus.
- Two callers with the same query text but DIFFERENT authorized project scope never share a coalesced scan or a cached result (singleflight/cache-key fixture with deliberately colliding query hashes and differing scope).
- A request whose caller-supplied filter widens beyond the caller's authorized scope is served only the authorized subset, never the wider requested one.
- Deadline shorter than scan time: route returns cancelled; TS caller degrades per auto-search semantics (hint skipped, no error surfaced to user).
- Daemon down: backend seam falls back to TS scan with one loud log; results still returned.
- Two identical concurrent queries from the SAME authorized scope: one inference + one scan (singleflight counters).
- Background backfill saturating queues: an interactive query is still admitted within reserved capacity (latency assertion under load).
- Cold start: first search after daemon restart serves fallback; post-warm search serves the Rust path (state visible via status route).

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace + bun test + hermetic e2e group green.
notes: reduce-complexity: unit is OVERSIZED (routes + authz + queues + fallback + facade) - noted per conversion constraints, not split; less-code: TsScanBackend reuses the existing scalar path behind the seam, no rewrite; perf: reserved interactive capacity asserted under load; ponytail-review: lean given R32/KTD25 key shape is load-bearing security, not a nicety; invariant-test-review: scope-isolation oracle uses deliberately colliding query hashes with differing scope - proves the R32 key shape, widened-filter test asserts served subset; test-strategy: hermetic e2e + counter-based singleflight oracles + adversarial fixtures

title: U14: Segment persistence + outbox consumer (push route)
description:
Phase 3. Crash-consistency tests are a hard gate for this unit (Verification Contract: crash suites for U14).

## Goal
Index generations survive restarts and stay fresh via the outbox — no full rebuild per insert — without the module opening context.db directly.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R14: "Vector index generations are immutable (base segment + bounded delta segments + tombstone bitmap), published atomically via a manifest; readers never observe a partial build, and old generations retire only after readers drain."
- R6 (transactional outbox maintenance), R31 (no new daemon; converge on existing machinery).
- KTD11: "Readers hold Arc<Mmap>-style generations; publish via manifest/ArcSwap; size-tiered compaction; per-segment local top-K merged at the end. Avoids full-generation rebuilds on every insert."
- KTD30: "U14's outbox consumer receives batches through a TS-initiated push route, not by the module opening context.db. The TS projection writer calls a vector.ingest route (established by U13) with pending outbox batches; the module writes segments and returns acknowledgment IDs; TS marks those outbox rows applied. crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs states the module never opens or attaches context.db, and that boundary changes only at U29's authority convergence — U14 does not anticipate it."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/segments.rs, src/manifest.rs (new)
- crates/mc-module/src/vector_search.rs; new vector.ingest route in crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs
- TS-side outbox drain in packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/retrieval-projection.ts

## Approach
1. Immutable base + bounded delta segments + tombstone bitmap; atomic manifest publish (fsync -> validate -> swap); readers pin generations; retire on drain; size-tiered compaction.
2. Per KTD30 (quoted above); acknowledgment is batched (no per-row transactions) on both sides.
3. Per-project/space byte-bounded residency with LRU eviction (replaces the process-global 256 MB decoded-pool behavior with an explicit budget).

## Test scenarios
- kill -9 between fsync and manifest swap: reopen serves the OLD generation intact (crash test with fault-injection points) — the R14 no-partial-reads oracle.
- Compaction removes tombstoned ordinals; post-compaction search equals pre-compaction search minus deletions (comparator).
- A reader holding an old generation during publish completes its scan on the old data; the next query sees the new generation.
- An outbox batch of N mutations pushed over vector.ingest lands in <= ceil(N/batch) transactions on the module side (statement counter), and applied_at marks EXACTLY ONCE on the TS side even under redelivery (idempotent ack test).
- The module process never issues a SQLite connection open against context.db during this unit's tests (process-level assertion) — the KTD30 boundary oracle.
- Eviction: exceeding the byte budget evicts the LRU project; the next query for it reloads from segments, correctness preserved.

## Verification
- cargo test; crash-consistency tests in CI; staleness SLA documented on the route (outbox consumed on search when pending, bounded added latency).
notes: reduce-complexity: segment machinery is R14-mandated; less-code: replaces the process-global 256MB decoded pool with one explicit budget; perf: batched acks kill per-row transactions (R29 direction); ponytail-review: no anticipation of U29 boundary change - module never opens context.db, held by process-level assertion; invariant-test-review: R14 no-partial-reads proven by kill-9 between fsync and manifest swap serving the OLD generation, exactly-once ack under redelivery; test-strategy: crash/fault-injection form + comparator + statement counters

title: U12: Kernel dispatch + top-K selection benchmarks
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
Runtime-dispatched kernels and a measured top-K structure choice.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R28: measure, do not assume — variants land only on measured wins.
- KTD2: safe-SIMD-first with "runtime-dispatched NEON and AVX2/FMA variants (AVX-512/VNNI only where deployed) and no blanket target-cpu=native".

- Dispatch on a host lacking a feature falls back cleanly (force-disable flag in tests).
- Top-K structures agree with a full-sort reference across K values and duplicate scores.

## Verification

notes: reduce-complexity: ok; less-code: losing top-K structures REMOVED after measurement, only the winner ships (no dead experiment code); perf: measured K-band selection is the whole point; ponytail-review: AVX-512/VNNI only where deployed (KTD2), nothing speculative built; invariant-test-review: exact-agreement oracle vs scalar comparator including duplicate-score ties, force-disable fallback test; test-strategy: comparator property harness reused from U10 + bench table

title: U10: mc-vector crate: exact engine + trait
description:
Phase 3 — Rust dense engine. Develops in parallel with Phase 2 against synthetic corpora; integration comes in U13. Ships no ranking change itself, but its criterion baseline is the R28 correctness comparator that U15 measures against.

## Goal
The ID-first exact engine exists as a standalone crate with the VectorIndex abstraction.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R9: "Hot-path dense search runs in Rust over contiguous normalized vectors and returns compact (ordinal, score) pairs; stable IDs, text, and metadata hydrate only after fusion selects final candidates."
- R12: "Exact search is the default engine. ANN (HNSW) is added only behind the VectorIndex abstraction when measured thresholds are crossed: auto-search p95 above ~25 ms or active decoded index above ~128 MB for a scope." This unit lands the abstraction SEAM only — no HNSW work.
- R14: in-memory generation shape (immutable generation + tombstones).
- KTD1: "Dense engine lives in a new crates/mc-vector crate, exposed as routes on the existing ck-mc module ... mc-vector depends only on workspace-internal crates (no subc/cortexkit deps) so it builds and benches in isolation."
- KTD2: "Safe-SIMD-first kernels with runtime dispatch. The workspace is #![forbid(unsafe_code)] everywhere; mc-vector starts with a safe SIMD abstraction (pulp or wide) over a portable scalar baseline ... Unsafe is admitted only if benchmarks prove the safe abstraction leaves large wins on the table."
- KTD3: "Shard-local top-K per worker, merge workers x K; cancellation checked between scan blocks; never a shared heap in the scan loop."
- KTD10: "Row-major f32 exact scan is the baseline and correctness comparator."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/ (new: src/lib.rs, src/generation.rs, src/scan.rs, src/topk.rs, src/scratch.rs, criterion benches under benches/)
- root Cargo.toml workspace member

## Approach
1. Generation structure: packed normalized f32 row-major matrix, stable_ids: Vec<u64> (cold), filter bitmaps, tombstone bitset, group ranges (compartment -> ordinal range), generation id. QueryScratch with scores, seen-epoch, touched list, fixed-capacity top-K.
2. Dense u32 ordinals internally; (ordinal, score) output; stable-ID conversion only after top-K.
3. Normalize on index, normalize query once, dot product only; shard-local top-K, merge workers x K on a dedicated compute pool (KTD3).
4. VectorIndex trait: search(partition, query, k, filters, deadline), build_generation(docs), publish_generation(gen); ExactIndex is the first impl.
5. Scalar reference implementation kept as the correctness comparator; safe-SIMD kernels via pulp/wide (KTD2).
Directional: exact top-K with stable tie-breaking (score desc, ordinal asc).

## Test scenarios
- Property-test comparison: random corpus (1k x {128,384,1024}), random queries — SIMD scan top-K equals the scalar reference EXACTLY under stable tie-breaking, with and without tombstones.
- Deleted (tombstoned) ordinals never appear in results.
- K > live corpus returns all live, sorted.
- Deadline expiring mid-scan returns a cancelled error, NOT partial results presented as complete.
- Zero-vector and duplicate-vector inputs behave (no NaN; duplicates tie-break by ordinal).
- cargo bench baseline recorded for the scan across the U5 matrix dims.

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace; cargo clippy -- -D warnings; criterion baseline committed as a snapshot for U15 comparisons.
notes: reduce-complexity: VectorIndex trait seam is R12-mandated for future ANN, not speculative; less-code: scalar reference doubles as the correctness comparator - not dead code; perf: criterion baseline IS a deliverable (R28 comparator); ponytail-review: no HNSW, no unsafe - both trigger-gated per plan; invariant-test-review: SIMD-vs-scalar exact-equality property oracle under stable tie-breaking, deadline test asserts cancelled error rather than silent partials; test-strategy: property-based comparator + example edge cases (zero-vector, duplicates, K over corpus)

title: U11: Bitmap filters + adaptive scan
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
Filters cut memory traffic, not just results.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R10: "Filtering (project, session, source type, trust, status, embedding space, time/ordinal range) uses bitmaps applied before or inside the scan so excluded vectors never touch the memory hierarchy; the scan strategy adapts to filter selectivity (dense masked scan, sparse gather, or segment skip)."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/filter.rs (new), src/scan.rs

## Approach
1. Bitmaps per project/session/source/trust/status/space + coarse ordinal/time ranges; raw bitsets for dense sets, Roaring-style containers for sparse; the crossover is MEASURED per architecture (bench, not assumed).
2. Strategy selection by allowed-set density: dense -> sequential masked scan; sparse -> set-bit enumeration + gather; range-restricted -> whole-segment skip via min/max metadata.

## Test scenarios
- Each strategy returns IDENTICAL results to the reference filter-then-scan for random filter sets at 0.1% / 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% selectivity.
- Segment-skip: a query restricted to an ordinal range touches only overlapping segments (assert via scan counters).
- Empty filter set returns empty WITHOUT touching vectors.
- Bench records bytes-touched per selectivity point — proves the R10 mechanism (excluded vectors are not read), not just output correctness.

## Verification
- cargo test; bench comparison in PR notes.
notes: reduce-complexity: three strategies are R10-mandated adaptivity; less-code: minimal; perf: bytes-touched counter proves the mechanism (excluded vectors never read), not just outputs; ponytail-review: raw-vs-Roaring crossover measured per architecture, not assumed - already gated; invariant-test-review: strategy-equivalence property vs reference filter-then-scan across selectivities + counter-based traffic oracle; test-strategy: property comparison + mechanism counters

title: U9: Reader re-pointing to claims
description:
Phase 2. Completes KTD4's coexistence exit.

## Goal
Search, mural, dreamer, and module state-sync read claim current-state through one API; the legacy write path retires.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R1 (immutable revisions).
- R8: the retirement step is a fence-bumped migration and follows the rollout order — ship all binaries with new version support first, then migrate.
- KTD4 (exit): "readers re-point incrementally (U9); ... the legacy write path retires in a later fence-bumped migration."

- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/mural/resolve-mural.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/dreamer/ (classify, map-memories, verify-gate, task-executor)
