title: U8: Retrieval projection, outbox, generations, embedding spaces
description:
Phase 2.

## Goal
The rebuildable search projection and its maintenance plumbing exist; embeddings become content-addressed and space-keyed.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R3: "Every search structure (FTS tables, vector matrices, retrieval documents) is a derived projection, rebuildable from authoritative tables; corruption or loss of a derived index never damages or disables authoritative memory."
- R4: "An embedding space is a full contract — provider, model revision, tokenizer revision, query/passage templates, pooling, normalization, dimensions, metric, max input tokens, chunking version, text-view version — not a model name."
- R5: "Vectors are content-addressed: one physical vector per (embedding space, text-view version, content hash); documents reference vectors through postings, and exact duplicates are scored once."
- R6: "Index maintenance flows through a transactional outbox plus per-scope generation counters; cache and index validity checks are single indexed point lookups, never COUNT(*)/MAX(id) corpus probes or wall-clock TTLs."
- KTD9: "A search_index_generation(scope_id, embedding_space_id, generation, row_count, checksum) row increments transactionally with every mutation; cache validation is one indexed point lookup. Two explicit modes: exact mode always scans the packed index; lexical-gated mode fetches vectors only for lexical candidate IDs — never decode a full pool to score a candidate subset. ... a generation is scoped to that full identity, so changing any one field opens a new space and a new generation rather than silently reusing vectors."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/retrieval-projection.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-memory-embeddings.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/project-embedding-registry.ts
- tests co-located (also touches embedding-cache.ts and compartment-chunk-embedding.ts staleness probes)

## Approach
1. retrieval_documents (entity_type/entity_id/revision_id, view_kind, title, identifiers, body, content_hash, trust_state, authority_rank, validity window); index_outbox (document, space, operation, applied_at); search_index_generation per KTD9; embedding_spaces normalizing what embedding_registrations holds PLUS every R4 identity field — ALL ELEVEN fields participate in the space's unique identity, not just the six embedding_registrations already tracks.
2. document_embeddings keyed (embedding_space_id, text_view_version, content_hash) with a postings table document<->vector (R5); migrate existing memory_embeddings / compartment_chunk_embeddings / git_commit_embeddings content into the new shape via REBUILD (they are derived; no data-loss concern), keeping old tables until U9 re-points readers.
3. Projection writer subscribes to claim/tool-event mutations through the outbox INSIDE the same transaction; a rebuild command regenerates the whole projection from authoritative tables (the R3 proof).
4. Replace the 60 s embedding cache TTL and the COUNT(*)/MAX(id) staleness probes with generation point-lookups (embedding-cache.ts, compartment-chunk-embedding.ts); implement exact vs lexical-gated fetch modes (KTD9).

## Test scenarios
- Claim revision insert produces exactly one outbox row and one generation bump in the SAME transaction (rollback removes both).
- Two documents with identical content hash in one space share one physical vector; postings expand both at retrieval.
- Rebuild-from-scratch on a corrupted projection reproduces IDENTICAL document set and content hashes (R3 rebuildability oracle).
- Generation check: mutation invalidates the cached pool via one point lookup; unchanged generation serves the cached pool with ZERO corpus probes (statement counter).
- Lexical-gated mode fetches only candidate vectors (assert decoded byte count << full pool).
- Pending-embedding documents are lexically searchable immediately (outbox row present, vector absent).
- Changing any ONE of the eleven embedding_spaces identity fields (e.g., chunking version or max input tokens) on an otherwise-identical registration produces a distinct space id and a fresh generation; vectors from the old space are never scored against the new space's query.

## Verification
- bun test; migration tests; a projection-rebuild e2e script run documented in the unit's PR.
notes: reduce-complexity: unit is OVERSIZED (projection + outbox + generations + spaces) - noted per conversion constraints, not split; less-code: old embedding tables kept only until U9 re-points readers, removal scheduled there; perf: generation point-lookups replace COUNT(*)/TTL corpus probes - hot-path win; ponytail-review: all eleven R4 identity fields now prevents silent vector reuse later, plan-mandated; invariant-test-review: R3 proven by rebuild-equality oracle, R6 by same-transaction rollback oracle, KTD9 modes by statement/decoded-byte counters; test-strategy: example + counter-based mechanism oracles

title: U7: Memories-to-claims backfill + dual-read
description:
Phase 2. The crash-injection suite for the write triple is a hard gate for this unit.

## Goal
Every existing memory row becomes a claim + revision; memories continues to serve unported readers as a maintained projection.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- KD3 / R8: "Existing memory rows migrate forward into claims; derived indexes rebuild from scratch" — two truth models forever is worse than one bounded migration.
- R1: immutable revisions.
- KTD4: "Claims migration is additive with dual-read ... memories becomes a maintained compatibility projection so search, mural, dreamer, module state-sync, and the mc-store mirror keep working unmodified; readers re-point incrementally (U9); duplicates collapse by normalized hash during coexistence; the legacy write path retires in a later fence-bumped migration."
- KTD21 (atomicity invariant): "U7's backfill runs in the migration transaction for corpora under the U5-measured scale threshold; above it, the lazy startup backfill (v22 pattern) applies, gated by schema_migrations_meta, with reads served from the memories projection until the backfill's completion checkpoint flips. The claim revision write, the memories projection update, and their outbox/generation side effects commit atomically in one transaction (in either backfill mode) — a crash between them must never leave the two reader surfaces disagreeing."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-memory.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-claims.ts
- migration test

## Approach
1. Backfill migration: each active/archived memory row -> claim (subject/scope from project + category + normalized_hash) + revision 1 (content, category); merged_from JSON arrays -> claim_evidence/merge lineage rows; supersession -> conflict/supersede relations; verification rows -> verification_events.
2. Protocol per KTD21 (quoted above). The scale-threshold value is set from U5's scale measurements, not guessed here.
3. Writes go claims-first: storage-memory.ts mutators create a revision and update the memories projection row in the SAME transaction as the outbox/generation bump — this triple never partially commits. Dedup by normalized hash prevents double-surfacing during coexistence.
Execution note: write characterization tests over storage-memory.ts mutators BEFORE rewiring them — this is legacy-shaped code with many consumers.

## Test scenarios
- Backfill of a seeded v78 DB (memories with counters, supersession, merges, verifications) produces claims whose revision-1 content hashes equal the source rows; row counts reconcile.
- Post-migration memory update creates revision 2 and updates the projection row; both reads (claims API, legacy getMemoriesByProject) agree.
- Dedup: identical normalized hash surfaces once in search during coexistence.
- Mural, dreamer classify, and state-sync smoke: existing co-located tests keep passing UNMODIFIED (projection compatibility).
- Crash simulation: interrupted lazy backfill (if that path is used) resumes idempotently.
- Crash injection at EVERY point inside the claims-first write triple (revision insert, projection update, outbox/generation bump): after recovery, the claims read and the legacy getMemoriesByProject read ALWAYS agree — neither observes a partial write (KTD21 atomicity oracle).

## Verification
- Full bun test for packages/plugin; packages/e2e-tests memory scenarios green; crash-injection suite for the write triple green.
notes: reduce-complexity: dual-mode backfill is KTD21-mandated, not accidental; less-code: characterization tests first prevent rework on legacy mutators with many consumers; perf: lazy backfill path keeps startup bounded above the scale threshold; ponytail-review: threshold value comes from U5 measurement, not invented here; invariant-test-review: KTD21 atomicity proven by agreement of BOTH reader surfaces after crash injection at EVERY seam of the write triple - proves the invariant, not just execution; test-strategy: fault-injection form chosen for the write triple, characterization + example tests for mutators

title: U6: Claims/evidence authoritative schema
description:
Phase 2 — Domain model and retrieval projection.

## Goal
The immutable domain model exists: projects, episodes, source spans, observations, claims, claim revisions, evidence links, conflicts, verification events.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R1: "A change to claim content creates a new immutable claim revision; indexed text is never mutated in place."
- R2: "Every claim revision links to its evidence: observations extracted from source spans, with extractor provenance and an independence key."
- R8: "Schema changes are forward-only and additive, honor the schema-version fence and the multi-process migration-on-open guard, and follow a documented binary rollout order; all pre-existing memory rows migrate forward into claims." Rollout order: ship ALL binaries (OpenCode plugin, Pi plugin, CLI, ck-mc) with new version support FIRST, then let the migration run.

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts (v79+; new tables land in the context.db TypeScript migration lane per KTD4)
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/storage-db.ts
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-claims.ts
- migrations-v79.test.ts (number per actual next version)

## Approach
1. Tables per the audit's recommended schema: projects (numeric id + canonical_identity unique, seeded from existing git:/dir: identity strings) + project_aliases; episodes; source_spans (content_hash, raw_artifact ref); observations (extractor run, independence key); claims (subject/predicate/scope keys, state, current_revision_id); claim_revisions (immutable content + content_hash, UNIQUE(claim_id, revision)); claim_evidence join; claim_conflicts; verification_events.
2. CHECK constraints on every state/relation enum; join tables instead of JSON ID arrays; numeric FKs.
3. Follow the migration checklist: fence bump, fresh-DB schema, ensureColumn, clearSession wiring for session-scoped tables, co-located migration test.
Patterns to follow: table-creation and rebuild patterns from v22/v49 migrations; storage-schema-helpers.ts.

## Test scenarios
- Fresh DB initializes at the new version with all tables and constraints (CHECK violation on a bad state string fails the insert).
- Upgraded v78 DB gains the tables; FK integrity assertion passes.
- projects seeding maps every distinct existing project_path identity to one numeric id; aliases resolve.
- Two revisions of one claim: revision 2 insert leaves revision 1 bytes UNCHANGED (R1 immutability oracle); current_revision_id CAS updates.
- Old binary simulation: schema fence refuses to open the migrated DB (fence test per schema-version-fence.test.ts convention).

## Verification
- bun test packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations-v*.test.ts; LATEST_SUPPORTED_VERSION lockstep test green.
notes: reduce-complexity: 9 tables is ESSENTIAL domain complexity (immutable claims model), not accidental; less-code: CHECK constraints + join tables replace app-level validation and JSON ID arrays - net simpler; perf: numeric FKs and indexed lookups by design; ponytail-review: schema-only unit, no speculative columns; invariant-test-review: R1 immutability proven by revision-2-leaves-revision-1-bytes-unchanged, fence proven by old-binary refusal simulation; test-strategy: migration example tests per repo convention

title: Select a benchmark-approved GPU model without mixing embedding spaces
description:
## Context
GPU availability can justify a larger or different embedding model, but model choice changes the embedding space. Hardware detection alone is not evidence that a model improves retrieval. Existing 3q5 tasks already own embedding-space identity, provider capabilities, judged evaluation, lazy backfill, and gated default swaps.

## Current State
- `packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/embedding-identity.ts:10-79` includes Synapse model and fingerprint in provider identity.
- `packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/embedding-synapse.ts` discovers one certified model and validates model/fingerprint/epoch/dimensions on every response.
- `magic-context-3q5.25` expands identity to the full embedding-space contract.
- `magic-context-3q5.27` benchmarks candidate models and owns any default swap.

## Desired State
Trusted startup selection chooses exactly one certified Synapse lane:
- GPU bundle/model when policy allows it, hardware and runtime eligibility pass, and the model is approved by `magic-context-3q5.27`.
- Certified CPU bundle/model under the documented unsupported/unavailable behavior.

The active lane publishes one exact model identity through the existing catalog and `models.list`. If CPU and GPU profiles differ in any embedding-space field, they use distinct space IDs, generations, vectors, and lazy backfills. Search never compares vectors across spaces.

## Implementation Guidance
Extend startup configuration and lane initialization. Reuse existing discovery, model metadata, destination model IDs, generation checks, shadow lane, and lazy backfill. Do not add request-time device/model selection or a general multi-model registry.

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **REUSE / EXTEND**.
- REUSE `magic-context-3q5.25` embedding-space identity and `.27` benchmark/cutover.
- EXTEND `SynapseConfig` and existing one-lane initialization only as specified by the forged plan.
- REUSE existing fallback-provider behavior only for explicit Synapse failure. Never persist fallback vectors under the Synapse identity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Startup policy is deterministic and testable for supported GPU, unsupported GPU, missing driver, invalid GPU bundle, invalid CPU bundle, and forced modes.
- [ ] GPU model activation requires a committed `magic-context-3q5.27` benchmark decision; otherwise the CPU model remains active.
- [ ] Catalog and `models.list` expose only the active certified lane and its exact execution/model identity.
- [ ] A model/profile change opens a new embedding space and generation; old vectors remain isolated and retire through existing lazy backfill/GC.
- [ ] Partial re-embedding serves lexical results for gaps and performs no cross-space cosine comparison.
- [ ] GPU disappearance across restarts selects the documented CPU path without relabeling old GPU vectors.
- [ ] Runtime GPU failure never causes same-request CPU substitution.
- [ ] No new model registry, benchmark harness, or recovery scheduler is introduced.

## Testing Strategy
Use a startup matrix with fake hardware/runtime probes, then run existing shadow/cutover fixtures against different model dimensions and fingerprints. Include downgrade and rollback across process restarts.

## Related Work
Hard dependencies: `magic-context-3q5.25`, `magic-context-3q5.27`, and bounded GPU runtime. Related: `magic-context-3q5.26`, `magic-context-pml.4`.

title: Package, diagnose, and smoke the certified GPU Synapse lane
description:
## Context
Hermetic fake-provider tests cannot prove that a GPU driver, ONNX Runtime execution provider, dependent native libraries, model bundle, and shutdown path work together on a real host. `magic-context-c50.8` already owns daemon startup, installed runtime paths, connection management, and CLI doctor behavior. GPU packaging must extend that work.

## Current State
- `packages/cli/src/lib/embedding-runtime.ts:219-363` probes installed ONNX Runtime binaries in a child process and formats doctor failures.
- `packages/plugin/scripts/smoke-mc-host-synapse.ts` drives authenticated discovery, all four operations, restart recovery, and SQLite receipt application.
- `docs/synapse-model-bundle.md` defines offline CPU bundle/runtime verification and production smoke inputs.

## Desired State
Supported installations include one exact, certified GPU runtime package and GPU model bundle, plus the certified CPU path. Doctor reports whether GPU policy is eligible and why it is not. Release smoke proves the selected GPU provider on real hardware with network disabled and proves CPU behavior on a host without eligible GPU support.

## Implementation Guidance
Extend `magic-context-c50.8` install/doctor ownership and the existing Synapse smoke. Reuse subprocess probing so a broken native provider cannot crash the CLI process. Keep native library paths and hashes in trusted installation metadata. Do not download drivers, ORT, CUDA, TensorRT, or models at runtime.

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **EXTEND**. Extend current ORT load probe, Synapse production smoke, bundle documentation, and daemon startup inputs. Do not create a second installer or standalone GPU daemon.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Package matrix names exact supported OS, architecture, GPU, minimum driver, ORT/provider build, dependent native libraries, and hashes.
- [ ] CLI doctor distinguishes no GPU, unsupported GPU, missing driver/library, provider-load failure, insufficient memory, invalid bundle, semantic-certification failure, and healthy GPU lane.
- [ ] Native probing runs in a disposable child process and returns redacted diagnostics.
- [ ] Offline real-GPU smoke passes authentication, discovery, query, batch, pending/pages, ambiguous replay, restart resubmission, atomic destination application, and shutdown cleanup.
- [ ] CPU-only smoke proves documented behavior when GPU is absent or unsupported.
- [ ] Forced GPU mode fails closed when eligibility fails; auto behavior follows the forged policy.
- [ ] Production smoke refuses toy bundles, placeholder hashes, unapproved models, wrong driver/runtime identity, and unexpected execution providers.
- [ ] Release evidence records latency, throughput, peak host/device memory, loaded native libraries, and feature graph.
- [ ] Documentation covers installation, policy, doctor output, rollback, model-space migration, and removal.

## Testing Strategy
Keep fake-probe cases in regular CI. Run real GPU smoke on labeled hardware with the exact packaged artifacts. Run CPU fallback smoke on a GPU-disabled or CPU-only host. Never skip production GPU smoke for a release that claims GPU support.

## Related Work
Depends on model selection and `magic-context-c50.8`. Consumes model approval from `magic-context-3q5.27`.

title: Add certified GPU Synapse execution and hardware-selected model lane
description:
## Context
PR 16 / `magic-context-c50.6` establishes one certified, CPU-only Synapse model behind `mc-host`. The next capability is optional GPU execution and, when approved hardware is present, use of a separately certified GPU-suitable embedding model.

Existing work already owns important parts of this change:
- `magic-context-3q5.25` defines embedding spaces as full identities.
- `magic-context-3q5.26` defines provider/token-aware batching and capacity descriptors.
- `magic-context-3q5.27` evaluates candidate models and gates any default swap on the judged benchmark.
- `magic-context-c50.8` owns daemon/runtime packaging and doctor integration.
- `magic-context-pml.4` later moves the wider embedding pipeline into Rust.

This epic must extend those contracts, not create a second model registry, benchmark framework, recovery queue, or embedding identity.

## Desired State
`mc-host` can start one certified Synapse lane on a supported GPU. Trusted startup configuration supplies certified CPU and GPU runtime/bundle candidates. Startup chooses one lane according to an explicit, documented policy and publishes its exact model, fingerprint, epoch, dimensions, and execution profile.

A different GPU model is eligible only after `magic-context-3q5.27` records an in-domain benchmark win. Switching models creates a distinct embedding space and uses existing lazy backfill/cutover behavior. CPU and GPU vectors never share an identity unless certification proves they are the same embedding space within the accepted tolerance.

CPU remains the supported fallback when GPU hardware, driver, runtime, or certified GPU bundle is unavailable. A failure must never write CPU vectors under a GPU model identity or vice versa.

## Scope
1. Forge the hardware-support, execution-provider, resource-envelope, fallback, and model-selection contract.
2. Extend the certified bundle/native-runtime identity to cover GPU execution and dependencies.
3. Run bounded GPU inference under existing job, cancellation, and shutdown ownership.
4. Select the benchmark-approved GPU model at startup without cross-space comparisons.
5. Package, diagnose, and smoke the certified GPU lane on supported hosts.

## Stop Conditions
- No request-selected model path, runtime library, device, or execution provider.
- No runtime download, mutable model registry, model hot reload, or persistent Rust job queue.
- No multi-GPU scheduling until measurements and a separate task justify it.
- No default-model change without `magic-context-3q5.27` benchmark evidence.
- No silent CPU/GPU substitution under one model identity.

## Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **EXTEND / REUSE**.

- Extend `SynapseConfig`, `Backend`, `OrtIdentity`, existing job limits, and incarnation tracker in `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/`; do not add a parallel service or queue.
- Reuse Synapse request keys, process-local jobs, `module_restarted`, ledger receipts, and atomic destination application unchanged.
- Reuse `magic-context-3q5.25` embedding-space identity and `magic-context-3q5.27` model evaluation/cutover. Do not add another model-selection database.
- Extend `magic-context-c50.8` runtime packaging and doctor surfaces.

## Success Criteria
- Supported GPU hosts can run an offline, certified Synapse lane through the existing four operations.
- Unsupported or unhealthy GPU hosts use the documented CPU behavior without identity confusion.
- GPU memory, concurrency, batch work, retained results, and shutdown are finitely bounded and tested at exact limits.
- A GPU-specific model activates only after benchmark approval and always opens a distinct embedding space when its contract differs.
- Bun and Node real-host smokes cover GPU selection, CPU fallback, restart, and destination receipt atomicity.

## Related Work
- `magic-context-c50.6`: CPU Synapse baseline.
- `magic-context-c50.8`: daemon/runtime packaging and doctor.
- `magic-context-3q5.25`: embedding-space identity.
- `magic-context-3q5.26`: provider capability and batching contract.
- `magic-context-3q5.27`: model evaluation and gated swap.
- `magic-context-pml.4`: future Rust ownership of the wider embedding pipeline.

title: Forge GPU execution and model-selection contract
description:
## Context
The shipped Synapse design deliberately allows only one CPU execution provider, one inference permit, and one owner-provisioned model bundle. GPU support changes native dependencies, memory ceilings, concurrency, shutdown cost, failure handling, and model identity. Choosing those mechanisms inside an implementation task would anchor the project before their operational cost is known.

## Current State
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs:56-191` verifies and commits one process-global ORT library, then builds FastEmbed with one intra-op CPU thread.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs:35-81` holds finite host-owned limits and one trusted bundle/ORT configuration.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs:140-160` uses one FIFO semaphore and an incarnation tracker for started native calls.
- `docs/synapse-model-bundle.md` explicitly certifies CPU-only execution and excludes accelerator features.

## Desired State
Produce an implementation-ready, adversarially reviewed plan for the smallest supported GPU profile. The plan must decide the first execution provider and platform matrix, define "GPU supported," measure the operational envelope, and specify deterministic CPU behavior when GPU eligibility fails.

The plan must keep one active Synapse lane per process. It must treat a different GPU model as a distinct embedding space and consume the model winner from `magic-context-3q5.27`, not select a model from public leaderboards or hardware alone.

## Required Decisions
- Initial provider/platform scope, such as CUDA only versus a broader matrix. Do not promise providers that cannot be packaged and tested.
- Trusted startup policy (`auto`, forced CPU, forced GPU, or smaller equivalent) and failure behavior for each mode.
- Hardware eligibility evidence: device, driver, execution-provider availability, model compatibility, and minimum usable memory.
- Exact native artifacts and hashes, including provider dependencies beyond the core ORT library.
- GPU memory accounting, batch/token limits, concurrency/stream count, admission, OOM classification, and shutdown drain bound.
- Whether CPU and GPU execution of the same bundle are one certified space or separate spaces. Require semantic evidence for any shared identity.
- Startup and runtime fault matrix. Never retry a request on a different model or execution profile under the original identity.
- Rollout, rollback, observability, doctor output, and real-hardware test matrix.

## Implementation Guidance
Run `plan-forge` for this feature. Include performance and footgun review. Derive peak resident CPU bytes, peak device bytes, host-to-device copies, work per batch, queueing delay, and worst-case shutdown drain at every proposed cap. Update child bead descriptions if the accepted plan changes their boundaries.

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **EXTEND**.
- Extend existing Synapse backend/config/lifecycle. No second service.
- Reuse existing embedding-space, benchmark, and lazy re-embed work in `magic-context-3q5.25` and `.27`.
- Reuse `magic-context-3q5.26` capability descriptors instead of inventing GPU-only batching metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Versioned plan records the selected provider/platform matrix and rejected alternatives.
- [ ] Operational envelope contains explicit CPU memory, GPU memory, batch, concurrency, queue, latency, and shutdown calculations.
- [ ] Plan defines auto/forced selection behavior and every fallback or fail-closed branch.
- [ ] Plan defines model and execution-profile identity, including when re-embedding is mandatory.
- [ ] Plan maps each implementation step to existing child beads and related 3q5/c50/pml work without duplicate ownership.
- [ ] Two adversarial review lanes plus consolidation complete with no unresolved critical finding.
- [ ] No production code changes land in this task.

## Related Work
`magic-context-c50.6`, `magic-context-c50.8`, `magic-context-3q5.25`, `magic-context-3q5.26`, `magic-context-3q5.27`, `magic-context-pml.4`.
notes: Deep research completed 2026-08-23. Committed at docs/research/embedding-model-selection-2026-08-23/ (entry point deep-research-results.md; plan phase3-plan.md; synthesis phase2-synthesis.md). Result: no model winner can be named before the in-domain campaign; evidence supports one Linux NVIDIA CUDA ONNX Runtime Synapse profile, separate execution/semantic identity by default, and exact recipe-aware evaluation. The plan now carries an architecture-open comparison benchmark specification: the incumbent pipeline is a baseline arm, FTS5 porter unicode61 plus bm25, fixed 0.7/0.3 fusion, source boosts, candidate depth, and the missing reranker are treatments under test, with 9 factors, 22 first-round arms, mandatory lexical-only and dense-only ablations, and latency, index cost, and footprint as separate gates. Critical gap remains independent in-domain candidate results and a stable judged population.

title: Extend Synapse certification for one GPU runtime profile
description:
## Context
Synapse currently certifies one CPU-only FastEmbed bundle and one hash-pinned dynamic ORT library. GPU execution adds an execution provider, provider dependencies, device requirements, and potentially a different model. Readiness must continue to mean that every byte and semantic choice is proven before requests are admitted.

## Current State
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/bundle.rs:167-229` confines and hashes every listed model/tokenizer artifact before construction.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs:56-115` verifies one ORT library and commits its process-global identity.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs:129-191` constructs and structurally/semantically certifies the CPU backend.
- `docs/synapse-model-bundle.md` documents exact CPU-only artifact and feature-graph requirements.

## Desired State
Extend the existing bundle/runtime contract with the minimum fields required by the forged plan to certify one GPU execution profile. Certification must bind model bytes, tokenizer behavior, output/pooling/truncation, execution provider, native runtime and provider dependencies, target/driver compatibility, and expected resource policy.

Requests and route identity must not select any path, device, model, or provider. Expected GPU artifact or compatibility failures either select the documented CPU startup path or disable Synapse according to startup policy. Magic Context remains routable.

## Implementation Guidance
### Files to Modify
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/bundle.rs`: extend strict manifest validation only where the plan requires it.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs`: extend committed runtime identity and pre-construction verification.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs`: extend trusted startup configuration, not request schemas.
- `crates/mc-host/tests/synapse_bundle.rs`: GPU-profile rejection and identity tests.
- `docs/synapse-model-bundle.md`: packaging and certification contract.

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **EXTEND**. Grow `VerifiedBundle`, `OrtIdentity`, `Backend::load`, structural probe, and semantic corpus. Do not create a parallel GPU bundle loader or second certification format.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] GPU model and runtime artifacts are path-confined, size-bounded, and hash-verified before provider/session construction.
- [ ] Runtime identity includes every native dependency required by the selected execution provider.
- [ ] Unsupported device, driver, provider, target, model, or runtime combinations fail before readiness with a stable redacted reason.
- [ ] CPU-only bundles remain valid without placeholder GPU fields.
- [ ] Request JSON cannot select model files, runtime libraries, device IDs, or execution providers.
- [ ] Structural and semantic certification detect wrong output, pooling, truncation, dimensions, non-finite vectors, and incompatible GPU results.
- [ ] Feature-tree tests prove only plan-approved accelerator features are reachable; runtime downloads remain unreachable.
- [ ] Existing CPU bundle and protocol tests remain green.

## Testing Strategy
Use fake runtime/provider probes for deterministic rejection coverage. Reserve real GPU execution for the release-smoke task. Keep one tiny fixture format unless the forged plan proves a second fixture is necessary.

## Related Work
Blocked by the forged plan. Coordinates with `magic-context-c50.8`; model identity and benchmark authority remain `magic-context-3q5.25` and `.27`.

title: Implement bounded GPU inference under existing Synapse lifecycle
description:
## Context
GPU inference introduces finite device memory, host-to-device copies, asynchronous native work, and longer non-interruptible failure paths. The current Rust job table and incarnation tracker already own admission, idempotency, route-independent work, and shutdown. GPU support must extend those owners rather than add another scheduler.

## Current State
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs:35-70` defines finite job, input, retained-result, and page limits.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs:140-160` serializes CPU inference with one semaphore and tracks every started native call.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/jobs.rs:184-243` rejects work when bounded admission is full and deduplicates equal request keys.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/jobs.rs:298-349` serves pending and ordered bounded result pages.

## Desired State
The existing Synapse backend can execute the certified model through the approved GPU provider. Admission and batching obey the forged CPU/device-memory envelope. Route loss still cancels only response waiting. Shutdown closes admission, cancels queued wrappers, synchronizes and joins every started GPU call, then releases model/runtime state.

A GPU runtime fault never reruns the request on CPU under the same model/job identity. The request fails under the existing protocol. Any CPU selection occurs at a later startup through the selection contract.

## Implementation Guidance
### Files to Modify
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs`: configure approved provider through existing backend construction.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs`: extend existing permit/tracker ownership using measured plan values.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/jobs.rs`: change only if the accepted envelope requires additional accounted bytes; retain one job table.
- Existing Synapse protocol/job/lifecycle tests: add exact-boundary and fault cases.

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **EXTEND / REUSE**. Reuse the current `EmbeddingEngine`, job table, canonical request key, one-inference idempotency, output reservation, semaphore, `TaskTracker`, shutdown callback, and `module_restarted`. No GPU-specific queue or public operation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Approved GPU provider executes all four existing operations without protocol changes or extra operations.
- [ ] Device memory, host staging memory, concurrent native work, admitted batches, and encoded output have finite host-owned limits with exact-limit and limit-plus-one tests.
- [ ] Interactive/background behavior consumes the provider capability contract from `magic-context-3q5.26`; no duplicate GPU-only capability descriptor is added.
- [ ] Same key/equal payload still performs one inference; conflicting payload remains `idempotency_conflict`.
- [ ] Route loss leaves admitted batch work pollable and never abandons a started GPU call.
- [ ] Shutdown waits for stream/device synchronization and all native joins before handler and instance-lock release, including deadline-overrun coverage.
- [ ] OOM, provider reset, device loss, malformed output, and native panic return stable bounded failures and publish no suspect vector.
- [ ] No request falls back from GPU to CPU under its original job, receipt, or embedding identity.
- [ ] CPU Synapse tests remain green.

## Performance Considerations
Use only caps and concurrency selected by the forged plan. Report throughput, p50/p95 latency, peak host bytes, peak device bytes, and shutdown drain on the target GPU. Do not add multi-stream or multi-GPU support without measured need.

## Related Work
Depends on GPU certification and `magic-context-3q5.26` provider capacity semantics. Wider Rust embedding ownership remains `magic-context-pml.4`.

title: Memory exposure/outcome telemetry (data accrual for utility learning)
description:
Prerequisite for any future utility learning (counterfactual replay, bandit ranking — both deliberately deferred). Log now so data accrues; no consumer yet.

## Scope

- memory_exposure: query, candidate set, selected/injected memories, policy/index generation, token cost, latency.
- Outcome proxies per task window: user correction observed, retries, tool failures, explicit memory citation.
- Local only, byte-bounded, same privacy posture as embedding measurement corpus.

Explicit non-goals for this task: no ranking changes, no utility scores, no replay. retrieval_count alone is a popularity feedback loop, not utility — this is the data that eventually replaces it.

title: Contradiction-first retrieval: evidence bundles for top claims
description:
Retrieval-side only, no new writes. For top-N claim results, run a cheap secondary lookup over the U6 claim_conflicts / supersedes / revision edges and return an evidence bundle instead of a bare claim: current claim + strongest counterevidence + superseded flag + newer-revision pointer.

Changes the objective from "most relevant memory" to "decision-robust evidence set" — the agent sees that a retrieved decision was later contradicted or superseded before acting on it.

## Gate

U4 contradictory-memory and superseded-decision query classes: contradiction-surfacing rate up, stale automatic-injection rate down, bounded added latency (one indexed lookup per top claim).

title: Cache-aware memory placement: offline simulation
description:
The magic-context-native optimization nobody else can copy: placement decisions that price prompt-prefix cache invalidation. Offline simulation ONLY — no runtime change in this task.

## Scope

Replay real session traces comparing placements: current heuristics | stable-only m[0] | utility-based m[0]/m[1] | retrieval-only for low-frequency memories. Objective per memory: expected_benefit = P(use) x consequence_of_forgetting - token_cost - P(change) x prefix_cache_bust_cost. Approved safety/correctness invariants hard-pinned, exempt from optimization.

## Measure

Prompt-cache reads/writes, total input tokens, retrieval page faults, memory-omission failures vs current placement.

## Decision

If simulated win over current heuristics is small, kill here — memories may already be stable enough that current placement is near-optimal. Runtime implementation is a separate task gated on this result.

title: Retrieval keys: question-indexed memory (benchmark-gated)
description:
One canonical payload, multiple retrieval keys. Keys cannot corrupt truth — malformed keys hurt only recall — making this the best effort/value ratio item from the future-enhancements review.

## Scope

- Dreamer task (offline, cheap/local-model friendly) generates 3-8 keys per verified memory: WHY / WHAT / temporal-change / rejected-alternative / exact-symbol / failure-signature forms, plus deterministic keys (symbols, paths, error names, commit refs).
- Keys indexed alongside the canonical payload; search matches keys, returns payload. Keys never alter or replace stored content.

## Gate

U5 harness, U4 corpus: Recall@10/20 + MRR vs payload-only baseline, specifically on vague-recollection, temporal, and exact-rich categories. Note: measure AFTER the U16 planner + bigram engine land — the planner may already close the vague-recall gap, in which case this dies cheaply.

title: Failure-signature memory: typed retrieval objects for errors and failed tests
description:
Compiler errors, stack traces, failed tests, and benchmark regressions should be typed, normalized retrieval objects — not prose hopefully recoverable from a large assistant message.

## Scope

- Deterministic normalization (no LLM): paths -> <PATH>, line numbers -> <LINE>, addresses -> <ADDR>, request ids -> <ID>, numerics selectively templated, generic frames dropped, project frames kept. Substrate: tool_events (U21 / magic-context-3q5.23, see its delta note).
- Store per signature: environment, symptoms, false leads, root cause, fix, validation, recurrence conditions. Root-cause/fix fields populated when a linked episode resolves (historian/dreamer), else signature-only.
- Retrieval: exact signature match first, fuzzy (normalized-token) second. Triggered when a new diagnostic matches a stored signature.

## Measure

Repeated-failure resolution time proxy: does a matching signature surface on recurrence? False-match rate on the U4 error-message query class.

title: JIT memory interrupts: action-triggered retrieval on tool hooks (warn-only)
description:
Most memory systems are query-triggered. The plugin sits on tool hooks — use the planned ACTION as the trigger.

## Scope

- Fast deterministic trigger classifier on planned tool calls: git push, migration-file edits, file deletion, schema changes, benchmark runs. No LLM on the hot path.
- On trigger: retrieve matching anti-memories, failure signatures, and relevant PROJECT_RULES; inject a compact warning fragment (auto-search-hints style, fragments only, never full content).
- Warn-only, never block. Hard per-turn interrupt budget. Hard latency budget on the hook path — if retrieval can't answer within it, skip silently.

## Measure

Prevented-repeat rate (anti-memory/failure-signature hit preceding an avoided repeat), false-warning rate, added hook latency p95. Kill criterion: false-warning rate makes users disable it.

title: F16 fence read-loop emissions before connection Goodbye
description: Finding: Shutdown queues connection Goodbye without a producer barrier for read-loop control/rejection emissions. Severity CONSIDER (P2), concurrency correctness. Files: crates/mc-host/src/runtime.rs, connection.rs, dispatch.rs/wire.rs and lifecycle tests. Shutdown freezes route admission and drains routes, but read loops can still start/finish catalog or server_busy terminals while shutdown queues Goodbye, allowing a terminal after Goodbye. Introduce a generation/read-loop emission fence or explicit producer join so every started control/rejection send completes before Goodbye and no later send begins. Extend the existing shutdown terminal-order test with deterministic barriers, confirm failure, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: All control/rejection emissions started before shutdown are queued before connection Goodbye; no read-loop emission can begin afterward; deterministic tests cover catalog and rejection races; generation teardown remains bounded; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified catalog response caching, one-deadline outbound admission, and read-producer fencing before Goodbye; focused and full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/strict lib-test clippy pass.

title: F15 bound outbound admission with one deadline
description: Finding: Outbound byte-budget and writer-queue waits are unbounded. Severity CONSIDER (P2), reliability. Files: crates/mc-host/src/dispatch.rs, wire.rs/config.rs and dispatch/wire/lifecycle tests. emit_frame waits separately for egress ByteBudget and writer queue with only generation cancellation; a live slow consumer can retain request/settlement resources indefinitely. Apply one absolute operation deadline across both admission waits, using existing timing policy where possible, and retire the generation on expiry. Extend existing stalled-writer/byte-budget tests with paused-time or deterministic barriers, confirm failure, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: Every outbound operation has one absolute deadline spanning byte charge and writer queue admission; deadline expiry retires generation and releases all charges/resources; deterministic tests cover both stages and prove the second receives only remaining budget; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified catalog response caching, one-deadline outbound admission, and read-producer fencing before Goodbye; focused and full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/strict lib-test clippy pass.

title: F11 reserve or cache catalog response before serialization
description: Finding: Catalog response memory is allocated before resident-byte reservation. Severity CONSIDER (P2), performance/correctness. Files: crates/mc-host/src/control.rs, runtime.rs, connection.rs and catalog tests. Every catalog.list builds a fresh serde_json Value/Vec before emit_frame charges output, so concurrent connections can allocate copies outside max_resident_bytes. Prefer serializing and validating immutable catalog variants once at startup, or reserve an exact conservative bound before serialization and transfer that charge. Extend existing catalog/control tests with deterministic allocation/reuse/accounting coverage, confirm the old behavior fails the new contract, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog serialization is cached at startup or fully reserved before allocation; repeated/concurrent catalog.list calls do not create uncharged full catalog copies; filters remain truthful and frame bounded; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified catalog response caching, one-deadline outbound admission, and read-producer fencing before Goodbye; focused and full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/strict lib-test clippy pass.

title: F10 enforce publication permissions independent of umask
description: Finding: Umask can strip required owner permissions. Severity CONSIDER (P2), correctness/security. Files: crates/mc-host/src/instance.rs and tests/instance_security.rs. Directory/file creation modes are masked by umask, so a restrictive umask may yield unreadable publication credentials even though creation through the fd succeeds. Explicitly fchmod every newly created private directory component to 0700 and publication/secret files to 0600 before publication, while retaining symlink/race defenses. Extend existing instance security coverage with a subprocess or serialized umask test, confirm it fails before the fix, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: New private directories are exactly owner rwx and credential/publication files exactly owner rw regardless of restrictive umask; no process-global umask test races; existing nofollow/identity cleanup defenses remain intact; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Resolved with explicit 0700/0600 fchmod behavior independent of umask. Added a subprocess test under umask 0777, confirmed the pre-fix open_component failure, then verified publication remains readable with exact owner modes. Instance unit/security tests pass.

title: Port git-commits ingestion to Rust
description: TS-only, zero Rust hits: git-commits/{indexer,git-log-reader,sweep-coordinator,storage-git-commit-embeddings}.ts — HEAD log reading, commit indexing, per-commit embeddings, sweep coordination. Port to Rust (gix or git2). Embedding leg depends on the embedding-pipeline port.
acceptance_criteria: Commit indexing + sweep runs in Rust; commit rows/embeddings written to Rust-owned store

title: Port message index to Rust (coordinate with 3q5 lexical indexes)
description: TS-only: message-index.ts, message-index-async.ts, maintenance + orphan sweep (dream-timer.ts:292-299) — raw-message index feeding ctx_search in both modes. Rust store has no FTS at all (LIKE-only search). 3q5 U17 builds dual lexical indexes for the retrieval overhaul; this task = make raw-message indexing a Rust-side source for that system rather than re-porting the TS FTS design. Mostly a design-alignment + implementation task, not a 1:1 port.
acceptance_criteria: Raw messages indexed Rust-side as a 3q5 retrieval source; TS message-index retired in rust mode

title: Decision: mural PNG rendering — port to Rust or keep host-side
description: Mural renderer is host-side BY DESIGN (mc-module lib.rs:7983); TS font-renders memory cues to PNG (mural/render-mural.ts), ships the data-URL inside the transform wire, Rust stores + injects it into m0. Porting means font rasterization in Rust (e.g. cosmic-text/fontdue + png). Decide: heavy enough to justify port vs deliberate host-side presentation concern. Record decision; spawn implementation task only if port chosen.
notes:
Decision (2026-08-19): KEEP mural PNG rendering host-side; do not port it to Rust.

Rationale:
- The PNG is an opaque presentation artifact. The host owns model-capability gating and host-specific image envelopes; the Rust module already owns frozen m0 composition plus hash-gated artifact persistence. Pi also consumes the shared TypeScript renderer, so a Rust port would not retire the host implementation.
- The feature is experimental, default-off, vision-gated, cue-coverage-gated, and overflow-gated. In the TypeScript path it normally runs only during HARD baseline materialization.
- A port would duplicate the 634-line deterministic layout/raster/PNG implementation, generated atlas, and parity suite while widening Rust memory snapshots and reconciling the plugin mural_manifest with mc_project_mural_artifacts. Different zlib encoders also make byte identity/versioning an explicit compatibility problem.
- The observed excess work is a host control-flow defect, not evidence that Rust should own rendering: render-trigger.ts calls renderMural before checking the stored text hash, so an unchanged mural still allocates/rasterizes/base64-encodes and runs level-9 deflate. Rust mode also resolves the mural before classification on every eligible primary transform rather than only on HARD/refold work.
- The cache identity hashes layout text only and has no renderer epoch, so palette/font/encoder changes can reuse stale PNG bytes. The existing rerendered=false test proves no DB upsert, not that rasterization/encoding was skipped.

Related Rust-mode correctness findings to preserve with this decision:
- render_config omits mural enablement, so toggle changes do not independently force the TS-equivalent HARD transition.
- A missing OpenCode mural payload does not clear the project artifact, allowing Claude Code to inherit stale imagery.
- Host resolution uses launch-scoped deps.projectPath before the session-derived identity and does not mirror the TypeScript memory-disabled project gate.

Preferred remediation before reconsidering ownership: split deterministic layout/cache identity from raster/encode; check the cache before pixel work; add a renderer epoch; align Rust-mode project, feature, memory, and stale-artifact gates; then profile cache misses and wire cost.

Revisit a Rust port only if post-remediation profiling shows material host latency/GC pressure, Rust becomes the sole/default execution path, Rust-only projects must create fresh murals without a host, or one Rust-owned artifact contract replaces both current stores.

No implementation child was spawned because the port was rejected, per this issue's task contract.
close_reason: Decision recorded: keep mural PNG rendering host-side. A Rust port would duplicate the renderer and host/Pi fallback while leaving the actual repeated-render/cache and Rust gating defects unresolved. Fix and profile the host path first; no implementation child spawned because the port was rejected.

title: Decision: smart-notes engine (condition compiler + sandbox runner) — port or keep TS
description: smart-notes/{compiler,condition-compiler,sandbox-runner,schedule,ssrf-guard}.ts compiles user conditions and executes them in a JS sandbox; Rust only stores notes + records evaluations (note.evaluate) and flags host capability note_evaluation_available (lib.rs:717). Rust port implies embedding a JS engine (boa/quickjs) or redesigning the condition language. Decide port vs keep-TS; security review of sandbox either way. Wake plane is magic-context-c50.7.
design: Retain the hardened TypeScript QuickJS compiler, sandbox runner, capabilities, and condition language as the sole evaluator implementation. Rust owns authoritative work selection, durable claims and replay, source/state/status revisions, lifecycle reduction, canonical persistence, protocol and authority fencing, and CAS. Integrate through a private client-initiated protocol-v2 evaluator worker with boot-ephemeral registration and zero-wait polling; magic-context-pml.3 owns later positive waits and scheduler orchestration.
notes: Implementation-ready plan: docs/plans/2026-08-19-0219-refactor-smart-note-evaluator-authority-boundary-plan.md (ignored by git under docs/plans/). The plan preserves the existing sandbox and egress contract, adds an atomic v2 cutover and authority handoff, and rejects a second Rust JavaScript engine or condition-language fork. Non-interactive document review applied two mechanical fixes; 6 proposed fixes, 6 decisions, and 1 FYI observation remain available for optional walkthrough. No implementation or tests were run during planning.
close_reason: Decision and implementation-ready plan completed: retain the TypeScript QuickJS evaluator and move authoritative selection, state, fencing, and CAS to Rust through the client-initiated protocol-v2 worker.

title: Port smart-notes wake plane (wake.create) or stub with fail-open
description: smart-notes/wake-plane.ts capability-gates standalone smart-note condition evaluation against the fleet wake plane (wake.create) with affirmative catalog detection, failing open on daemon connection failures. Decide: hand-roll wake.create in mc-host, or rely on documented fail-open and mark unsupported. Small surface; decision + implementation in one task.

title: U29: Authority convergence (embeddings + indexes)
description:
Phase 7. Convergence is an OWNERSHIP TRANSFER, not a capability removal: TS mode (authority TS, rust mode off) keeps the full TS pipeline working (R13).

## Goal
One writer, one embedding runtime, one index owner per the audit's end state — via the existing machinery.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R31: "Write ownership for memory domains, embedding generation, and vector indexes converges on the existing module-authority machinery (subc daemon + ck-mc module + authority domains); no new daemon is introduced."

- KTD30 boundary handoff: the module's never-opens-context.db boundary "changes only at U29's authority convergence" — this is that unit.

- crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs
- packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-state-sync.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/embedding-synapse.ts

## Approach
1. Extend authority domains beyond memories/notes to cover the retrieval projection, embedding generation, and vector-index ownership: prepare -> seed -> drain -> MODULE, reusing the existing state machine, guard triggers, and mirror protocol.

title: U28: Typed delta journal + checkpoints
description:
Phase 7. HARD SHIP CONDITION (KD4): this unit ships ONLY with the fault-injection crash/schema-evolution suite green — risk is paid with the dedicated test suite, not deferred.

## Goal
Steady-state persistence is O(delta), crash-safe, schema-evolvable.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R30: "Session-state persistence moves from full JSON rewrites to an append-only typed delta journal with periodic versioned checkpoints, changing steady-state persistence from O(total state) to O(delta), backed by crash-recovery and schema-evolution tests."
- KD4: "The append-only delta journal + checkpoint work is in active scope ... risk is paid with a dedicated crash/schema-evolution test suite."
- KTD14: "The delta journal is append-only typed deltas + periodic versioned checkpoints, replacing full JSON CoreState rewrites; it ships only with a crash/schema-evolution test suite (fault-injection points around append, checkpoint, truncate, replay)."
- Plan risk note: "Crash mid-append/mid-checkpoint must never lose acknowledged state."

## Key files
- crates/mc-store/src/journal.rs (new)
- crates/mc-store/src/lib.rs (CoreState persistence seam)
- crash-test suite crates/mc-store/tests/journal_crash.rs (new)

## Approach
1. Append-only typed delta records (versioned enum, forward-compatible decoding) replacing full JSON CoreState rewrites; periodic versioned checkpoints; recovery = load checkpoint + replay tail; journal truncation only AFTER checkpoint fsync.
2. Schema evolution: unknown-newer record versions fail closed (fence semantics consistent with the repo's fail-closed convention); checkpoint version gates replay.
3. Fault-injection points around append, checkpoint write, truncate, and replay; the unit ships only with this suite green (KD4 condition).

## Test scenarios (chosen form: fault-injection crash suite + property-style interleaving tests)
- Crash between append and ack: replay yields the last-acknowledged state EXACTLY (no phantom or lost deltas), across injected crash points at every seam.
- Torn/partial trailing record on replay is detected and truncated WITHOUT corrupting prior state.
- Checkpoint + truncate crash-interleavings never lose acknowledged deltas (property-style interleaving tests).
- Old-format checkpoint + new binary replays; new-format + old binary fails closed LOUDLY.
- Steady-state bytes written per simulated transform pass drop vs the JSON rewrite baseline (measured assertion — this is the Success Criteria order-of-magnitude claim's harness fixture).

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace including the crash suite; e2e Rust harness scenario green; persistence-bytes measurement in the PR.
notes: KD4 hard condition: ships ONLY with the fault-injection suite green; reduce-complexity: checkpoint+replay is the essential shape for O(delta) persistence; less-code: deletes full-JSON CoreState rewrites; perf: order-of-magnitude persistence-bytes drop is a measured assertion (Success Criteria); ponytail-review: fail-closed version fence matches repo convention, no speculative migration machinery; invariant-test-review: no-phantom-no-lost-deltas oracle at EVERY injected seam, torn-record truncation preserves prior state, old/new format matrix fails closed loudly; test-strategy: CHOSEN FORM per gate review - fault-injection crash suite (journal_crash.rs) + property-style checkpoint/truncate interleaving tests, per KD4

title: U27: Storage actor in mc-store
description:
Phase 7 — Storage and authority convergence. mc-store internal; no context.db involvement.

## Goal
One owner for the writer connection; interactive writes stop competing with maintenance.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R29: "A single storage actor owns each writer connection: bounded interactive and maintenance queues, weighted-fair scheduling, adaptive group commit, batched outbox delivery/acknowledgment, and deserialization outside transactions."
- KTD14 (placement): "The storage actor and delta journal live in crates/mc-store (the Rust store already has the single-writer lease and the outbox)."

## Key files
- crates/mc-store/src/lib.rs (actor module extraction), tests inline per crate convention

## Approach
An actor owning the write connection with bounded interactive and maintenance queues, weighted-fair scheduling, adaptive group commit (batch small writes per fsync window), batched outbox delivery/acknowledgment (replacing multiple reads and transactions per delivered row), deserialization outside transactions, and a WAL read pool for independent readers.
Execution note: write characterization tests around CURRENT outbox delivery semantics FIRST; the refactor must preserve exactly-once acknowledgment.

## Test scenarios
- Group commit: N small writes complete in << N fsync-equivalent transactions (transaction counter) with ALL writes durable after crash-point replay.
- Fair scheduling: a maintenance flood does not delay an interactive write beyond its budget (latency assertion under load).
- Outbox batch delivery acknowledges EXACTLY ONCE under redelivery/crash injection.
- Queue overflow applies backpressure (bounded), never unbounded memory growth.
- Read pool serves consistent snapshots during heavy writes (WAL semantics test).

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace; existing mc-store tests unmodified and green.
notes: reduce-complexity: actor extraction from existing lib.rs, no new crate; less-code: characterization tests around CURRENT outbox semantics first - refactor must preserve exactly-once ack; perf: group commit + batched acks + deserialization outside transactions are the R29 wins; ponytail-review: WAL read pool reuses SQLite WAL semantics, nothing invented; invariant-test-review: exactly-once ack proven under redelivery/crash injection, durability proven by crash-point replay, backpressure proven bounded; test-strategy: characterization first, then fault-injection + transaction-counter oracles

title: U26: Model evaluation + gated default swap
description:
Phase 6. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; the default encoder changes ONLY on an in-domain judged benchmark win (KD5, R25). A default change (if any) is its own reviewed PR citing the committed report.

## Goal
The default encoder is chosen by in-domain evidence.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R25: "The default embedding model changes only on an in-domain judged benchmark win; evaluation covers at minimum the MiniLM baseline, BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, nomic-embed-text-v1.5 at 256/512 dims, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B at 256/512 dims, and a BGE-M3 experimental lane, each with correct query/document instructions."
- KD5: "The embedding default stays Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 until a candidate wins the in-domain judged benchmark" (chosen over pre-selecting from public leaderboards).
- KTD7: "Model-swap invalidation: generation bump discards mismatched query vectors immediately (existing generationIsCurrent check); stored vectors purge lazily via background re-embed; search serves lexical-only for not-yet-re-embedded documents. No bulk synchronous purge."

## Key files
- shadow-lane configuration (project-embedding-registry.ts)
- benchmark runs (packages/plugin/scripts/benchmark-retrieval.ts)
- decision record appended to the benchmark snapshots

## Approach
Register each candidate (BGE-small-en-v1.5; nomic v1.5 at 256/512; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B at 256/512; BGE-M3 experimental) as a shadow space with correct instructions/templates; run the judged benchmark per space; a winner must beat MiniLM on the quality metrics WITHOUT violating latency/footprint criteria. Rollout of a winner: the new space becomes primary for new embeddings, lazy background re-embed migrates history, lexical-only serves the gap (KTD7).

## Test scenarios
- Shadow lane produces vectors under the candidate's declared space id and instructions (fixture asserting template application per candidate).
- Swap rollout: after the primary flip, search on a partially re-embedded project returns fused results with unembedded docs in lexical lanes only — NO cross-space cosine comparisons (generation check).
- Rollback of a candidate (deregistration) leaves the primary space untouched and search consistent.

## Verification
- Benchmark reports per candidate committed; the default change (if any) is its own reviewed PR citing the report.

title: U24: Embedding-space contract + purpose plumbing
description:
Phase 6 — Embedding spaces and evaluation.

## Goal
Spaces are identities, not model names; purpose reaches the encoder; every provider path carries an explicit trust-boundary contract.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R4: an embedding space is the full eleven-field contract, not a model name.
- R24: "The query-vs-passage purpose is honored end to end: unifiedSearch defaults to query purpose, and the local provider applies purpose templates instead of ignoring the parameter." (This unit does the provider-side template work; the default flip is U30.)
- R26: provider-aware batching groundwork (capability descriptors land fully in U25).
- KTD26: "Embedding providers carry an explicit trust-boundary contract: permitted outbound data is limited to the text being embedded (never full claim or tool-event context beyond the chunk in flight), TLS is required for every remote provider, provider-side retention/training opt-out is a registration precondition where the provider exposes the control, and provider credentials live in the existing secret-management path (never inline config) with rotation on the same cadence as other external-service credentials."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/embedding-local.ts
- memory/embedding-provider.ts
- project-embedding-registry.ts (+ tests)

## Approach
1. Local provider applies query/passage templates per space definition instead of ignoring purpose; the MiniLM space declares max input 256 word pieces (its true truncation) so the chunker budget matches reality.
2. Registry rows migrate onto embedding_spaces (U8 schema); generation semantics key on space id; two configurations of one model with different templates are DISTINCT spaces.
3. Each provider registration declares a trust-boundary contract per KTD26 (quoted above).

## Test scenarios
- Provider called with "query" vs "passage" produces template-differentiated inputs for a template-bearing space (tokenizer input spy); the MiniLM space remains symmetric (identical).
- Chunker respects the space's max input (no window exceeding 256 word pieces for MiniLM).
- Same model + different query template resolves to two space ids; vectors never cross-compared (generation check fixture).
- Registration migration maps every existing registration to a space row losslessly.
- A remote-provider registration without TLS, or with credentials supplied inline rather than through the secret-management path, FAILS registration validation.
- The embedding payload sent to a remote provider contains ONLY the chunk being embedded, never adjacent claim or tool-event context (payload-content assertion against a fixture with adjacent sensitive context).

## Verification
- bun test; shadow measurement runs unaffected.
notes: reduce-complexity: ok; less-code: registry rows migrate onto the U8 schema, no parallel registry; perf: MiniLM true 256-word-piece truncation declared so the chunker budget matches reality; ponytail-review: lean given KTD26 trust-boundary contract is load-bearing; invariant-test-review: template differentiation proven by tokenizer input spy, TLS/inline-credential registrations FAIL validation, payload assertion proves only the chunk in flight leaves; test-strategy: spy-based examples + negative registration tests + payload-content fixture

title: U21: tool_events source
description:
Phase 5. Ships under the new fusion only (KTD6) — tool events are a new source and never enter the legacy scoring path. Redaction and untrusted-provenance labeling are LOAD-BEARING, not optional hardening (plan risk note: "skipping them would let a credential fragment reach a provider through an auto-search hint").

## Goal
Compiler errors, test failures, diffs, and command outputs become retrievable evidence, redacted before indexing and marked untrusted before they reach a hint.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R21: "Tool events are a first-class searchable source: the raw artifact is stored once under a content hash, extracted metadata and salient text are indexed, tool-call/result pairing and file paths/symbols/error codes/test names are preserved, and results point back to the raw artifact."
- R33: "Tool-event content is redacted for known secret patterns before indexing, using the shared redaction utility, and carries an explicit untrusted-provenance state distinct from claims; auto-search renders tool-event content as delimited, provenance-marked evidence, never as unmarked instruction-bearing text."
- KTD12: "Tool events capture at the tool execution lifecycle hooks (hook-handlers.ts already observes tool lifecycle). Raw artifacts are content-addressed and stored once; indexing extracts file paths, symbols, error codes, test names, and salient text; large outputs are chunked; nothing embeds megabytes wholesale."
- KTD27: "extracted text and salient chunks get secrets replaced with typed placeholders (e.g., [REDACTED:api_key]) that stay searchable by type without leaking the value; the raw content-addressed artifact keeps the original content for the owning user but is never surfaced in search results or auto-search hints unredacted ... clearSession and any future retention policy cover the raw artifact and every derived projection, not just the tool_events row." Auto-search renders tool-event content as delimited, provenance-marked evidence because an attacker-controlled command result or repo file could otherwise inject instructions into the model's context once indexed.
- KTD28: U22's chunker lands first; this unit's large-output path delegates to it.

## Key files
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/tool-events/ (capture, storage, extraction; + tests)
- packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/hook-handlers.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- projection wiring in retrieval-projection.ts
- packages/plugin/src/shared/redaction.ts (REUSED, not reimplemented)

## Approach
1. tool_events table per the audit shape (tool name, operation, normalized input/output, exit status, file paths, content hash, episode/session/project, occurred_at); raw artifact stored once content-addressed alongside source_contents conventions.
2. Capture at tool execution lifecycle hooks; normalization strips volatile noise (timestamps, absolute temp paths) before hashing. Per KTD27: extracted text and salient chunks pass through the shared redaction utility BEFORE indexing. Extraction pulls file paths, symbols, error codes, test names into the identifier index; large outputs chunk via U22's boundary segmenter; retrieval results carry a pointer to the raw (unredacted, access-scoped to the owning user) artifact.
3. Ships under the new fusion only (KTD6); capture is bounded (size caps per event, drop-with-log over cap).
4. Tool events carry an explicit untrusted-provenance trust state distinct from claims; auto-search renders their content as delimited, provenance-marked evidence in hints, never as unmarked instruction-bearing text.
5. clearSession and any future retention policy cover the raw artifact AND every derived projection (indexed text, embeddings), not just the tool_events row.

## Test scenarios
- A failing-test tool result is retrievable by its error code and by test name via the identifier lane; the result links back to the intact raw artifact.
- Identical repeated command output stores one artifact (content-hash dedup) with two event rows.
- Megabyte output: only extracted/salient chunks embed (embedding-call counter), full raw stored, over-cap event dropped loudly.
- Tool-call/result pairing preserved (query returns the pair context).
- Tool output containing a seeded API key/bearer token: extracted indexed text carries a redaction placeholder; the raw artifact retains the original for the owning user; an auto-search hint for a related query NEVER contains the secret value.
- An auto-search hint built from a tool event renders it as delimited, source-labeled evidence, distinguishable from claim-derived content in the same hint.
- Session deletion cleans owned tool events, their raw artifacts, AND their derived index/embedding entries (clearSession wiring covers all three).

## Verification
- bun test; e2e scenario: run a session with tool activity, ctx_search finds the diagnostic without leaking a seeded secret. Migration discipline gates apply (new table).
notes:
reduce-complexity: unit is OVERSIZED (capture + storage + extraction + redaction + retention) - noted per conversion constraints, not split; less-code: REUSES shared redaction.ts and U22 chunker, no reimplementation; perf: capture bounded with size caps, drop-with-log over cap, nothing embeds megabytes wholesale; ponytail-review: lean given R33 redaction and untrusted-provenance are load-bearing security, not hardening; invariant-test-review: seeded-secret oracle proves the full chain (placeholder in index, original in raw artifact, secret NEVER in a hint), clearSession covers all three surfaces; test-strategy: e2e session scenario + seeded-secret fixtures + counter-based embed-volume oracle
DELTA (future-enhancements review): tool_events is the substrate for failure-signature memory (see follow-up task). Store a normalized signature alongside the raw event (paths -> <PATH>, line numbers -> <LINE>, addresses -> <ADDR>, request ids -> <ID>, generic frames dropped, project frames kept) so signature retrieval never rescans raw payloads.

title: U23: Bound-driven hierarchical retrieval
description:
Phase 5. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes, and the Verification Contract lists this unit under the retrieval benchmark gate; a direct U5 dependency edge exists (adjudicated — see notes) because no other dependency path reaches U5.

## Goal
Lifetime history search cost is bounded without recall loss.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R22: "Compartment retrieval is hierarchical and bound-driven: per-compartment centroid(s) plus a maximum residual radius give a provable upper bound (q.x <= q.centroid + r for unit q), groups are searched in descending bound order with an exact top-K stop rule, and heterogeneous groups are split."
- KTD13: "Hierarchical retrieval is bound-driven, not fixed top-N. Per-compartment centroid(s) + max residual radius stored with the index's group ranges; groups traversed in descending upper-bound order; stop when the next bound cannot beat the current k-th exact child; heterogeneous groups split. Preserves exact top-K, unlike a top-20-parents heuristic that can miss a minority topic."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/hierarchy.rs (new)
- summary-vector maintenance in the projection/outbox path
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/compartment-chunk-embedding.ts

## Approach
1. Per-compartment centroid(s) + max residual radius maintained on chunk mutation (incremental where possible); stored with the generation's group ranges.
2. Group traversal in descending q.centroid + r order; stop when the next bound cannot beat the current k-th exact child; heterogeneous groups (large r) split; leaf scans only within admitted groups; union with global lexical results.

## Test scenarios
- Exactness property: hierarchical top-K EQUALS flat exact top-K on randomized corpora (the comparator, many seeds).
- Pruning effectiveness: a clustered corpus scans a small fraction of leaves (scan counter bound asserted); an adversarial uniform corpus degrades gracefully to near-flat scan, STILL CORRECT.
- A minority topic inside a broad compartment is found (the fixed-top-N failure case as a regression fixture).
- Centroid/radius stay correct across chunk insert/delete (recomputed vs incremental parity).

## Verification
- cargo test; benchmark leaf-scan reduction at the 100k scale point recorded.
notes: judge-ruling: direct U5 dependency edge ADDED - this unit is benchmark-gated (Verification Contract) but had NO other dependency path to U5; adjudicated by opposing analysts + judge: fix the one real gap, keep U17/U19/U20 transitive; reduce-complexity: bound-driven traversal is KTD13-mandated over the simpler-but-wrong top-N heuristic; less-code: minimal; perf: leaf-scan reduction recorded at the 100k point; ponytail-review: exactness preserved - not speculative machinery, it is the recall guarantee; invariant-test-review: exactness property (hierarchical == flat exact, many seeds) + adversarial uniform corpus stays CORRECT + minority-topic regression fixture; test-strategy: randomized property comparator chosen as primary form + scan-counter pruning oracle

title: U22: Retrieval-aware chunking + content addressing
description:
Phase 5 — Corpus enrichment. BUILD ORDER (KTD28): this unit lands BEFORE U21 — "U21's large-output path explicitly needs U22's chunking machinery; building U21 first would force a throwaway duplicate chunker."

## Goal
Chunks follow structure; local edits stop re-embedding suffixes; content addressing pays measurably; U21's large-output path has chunking machinery to call.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R23: "Chunk boundaries prefer structure (episode, user/assistant turn, tool-call/result pair, code or diagnostic block, paragraph, sentence) with content-defined chunking for stability; message ordinals live in mapping metadata, never inside hashed text, so local edits do not re-embed the suffix."
- R5: content-addressed vectors (one physical vector per (space, text-view version, content hash)).

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/compartment-chunk-embedding.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/recursive-text-splitter.ts (fallback role)
- new boundary segmenter module (+ tests)

## Approach
1. Boundary hierarchy above the recursive splitter: episode -> user+assistant turn -> tool-call/result pair -> code/diagnostic block -> paragraph -> sentence -> character fallback.
2. FastCDC/Gear-style content-defined cut points over semantic-unit hashes constrained by min/target/max token sizes; ordinals in mapping metadata, NOT hashed text; shared parent ID for overlapping chunks so duplicates do not dominate packing.
3. Measure duplicate rate on real corpora FIRST (script) — content addressing beyond exact-hash stays out if repetition is low (trigger-gated by measurement, per plan).

## Test scenarios
- Editing one message mid-history changes only nearby chunk hashes; suffix chunk hashes stay STABLE (golden corpus assertion) — the R23 no-suffix-re-embed oracle.
- Boundary preference: a tool-call/result pair never splits mid-pair when it fits the window.
- An oversized single unit falls through to the recursive splitter, then char fallback (termination guaranteed; existing splitter tests still pass).
- Ordinal metadata maps every chunk back to its exact span; overlap chunks share a parent ID and dedup in packing (ties to U19).

## Verification
- bun test; re-embed volume on the edit fixture drops vs current windowing (measured in the PR).
notes: KTD28: lands BEFORE U21 - U21 large-output path delegates to this chunker; reduce-complexity: boundary hierarchy sits ABOVE the existing recursive splitter (fallback role), no rewrite; less-code: content addressing beyond exact-hash stays OUT unless the duplicate-rate measurement justifies it - plan-gated; perf: suffix-stable hashes cut re-embed volume, measured in PR; ponytail-review: measure-first step 3 is the lazy path, keep; invariant-test-review: R23 proven by suffix-hash stability golden + never-splits-mid-pair boundary oracle + guaranteed termination; test-strategy: golden corpus assertions + fallback-termination examples
